qs.e: Initial PE = m·g·h = 500 × 10 × 20 = 100,000 J. Final KE = ½·m·v² = ½ × 500 × (18)² = 250 × 324 = 81,000 J. Mechanical energy lost to friction = PE_initial - KE_final = 100,000 - 81,000 = 19,000 J.

qs.q: A hydraulic press has a pump piston of diameter 2.0 cm and a heavy ram piston of diameter 20.0 cm. If the machine operates at an efficiency of 85%, calculate the actual load force raised on the ram when an effort of 100 N is applied to the pump piston.
qs.e: Ideal Velocity Ratio VR = (D_ram / d_pump)² = (20.0 / 2.0)² = 10² = 100. Mechanical Advantage MA = VR × Efficiency = 100 × 0.85 = 85. Actual Load = MA × Effort = 85 × 100 N = 8500 N.

qs.q: Two identical parallel vertical springs each of force constant k = 300 N/m support a suspended mass of 12.0 kg. Calculate the total elastic potential energy stored in the two-spring system (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Parallel combination equivalent spring constant K_eq = k1 + k2 = 300 + 300 = 600 N/m. Total weight force F = m·g = 12.0 kg × 10 m/s² = 120 N. Total extension e = F / K_eq = 120 N / 600 N/m = 0.20 m. Total elastic energy E = ½·K_eq·e² = ½ × 600 N/m × (0.20 m)² = 300 × 0.04 = 12.0 J? Wait! Let's check: 300 * 0.04 = 12 J. Options: 12.0 J, 24.0 J, 6.0 J, 4.8 J.

qs.q: A mercury U-tube manometer has oil of density 800 kg/m³ in one arm and water of density 1000 kg/m³ in the other. If the mercury levels in both limbs are at equal heights, what is the ratio of the oil column height to the water column height?
qs.e: Equal pressure at interface: h_oil · ρ_oil · g = h_water · ρ_water · g => h_oil / h_water = ρ_water / ρ_oil = 1000 / 800 = 1.25.

qs.q: A submarine of total displacement volume 500 m³ floats in seawater (density 1025 kg/m³) with 20% of its volume above water. What mass of water ballast must be flooded into its tanks to achieve neutral buoyancy completely submerged?
qs.e: Volume of ballast water needed = volume exposed above surface = 20% of 500 m³ = 0.20 × 500 m³ = 100 m³. Mass of ballast water = V × ρ_seawater = 100 m³ × 1025 kg/m³ = 102,500 kg.

qs.q: Two spherical raindrops A and B fall through calm air at their respective terminal velocities. If the radius of raindrop A is twice the radius of raindrop B, calculate the ratio of the terminal velocity of A to that of B.
qs.e: By Stokes' law, terminal velocity v_t ∝ r². Ratio v_A / v_B = (r_A / r_B)² = (2 / 1)² = 4 : 1.

qs.q: Calculate the total heat energy required to convert 1.0 kg of ice at -10 °C into steam at 100 °C (c_ice = 2100 J/kg/K, L_f = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg, c_water = 4200 J/kg/K, L_v = 2.26 × 10⁶ J/kg).

An air bubble released from the bottom of a freshwater lake 20.0 m deep rises to the surface where temperature is the same as at the bottom. If atmospheric pressure is 10.0 m of water equivalent, calculate the ratio of the bubble's volume at the surface to its volume at the bottom.
qs.e: Pressure at bottom P1 = P_atm + h = 10 m + 20 m = 30 m water. Pressure at surface P2 = P_atm = 10 m water. By Boyle's law at constant T: P1·V1 = P2·V2 => V2 / V1 = P1 / P2 = 30 / 10 = 3 : 1.

qs.q: A wire fixed at both ends has length 1.2 m and vibrates in its 3rd harmonic (3 antinodes) at a frequency of 300 Hz. Calculate the speed of transverse waves along the wire.
qs.e: For 3rd harmonic L = 3·(λ/2) => 1.2 m = 1.5 λ => λ = 1.2 / 1.5 = 0.80 m. Wave speed v = f × λ = 300 Hz × 0.80 m = 240 m/s.

qs.q: An observer moves at a speed of 15 m/s towards a stationary sound source emitting a tone of 500 Hz. If the speed of sound in calm air is 335 m/s, calculate the frequency observed.
qs.e: Doppler effect for moving observer approaching stationary source: f' = f · [(v + v_o) / v] = 500 Hz × [(335 + 15) / 335] = 500 × (350 / 335) = 522.388 Hz ≈ 522.4 Hz.

qs.q: A thin transparent oil film (refractive index n = 1.40) floats on water (refractive index = 1.33). Monochromatic light of wavelength 560 nm in air is incident normally. Calculate the minimum non-zero thickness of the film for destructive interference in reflected light.
qs.e: Phase change of π occurs only at top surface (air n=1.0 to oil n=1.40), not at bottom surface (oil n=1.40 to water n=1.33). Condition for destructive interference in reflection: 2·n·t = m·λ. For minimum non-zero thickness m = 1 => 2 × 1.40 × t = 560 nm => 2.80 t = 560 => t = 200 nm.

qs.q: Calculate the critical angle for light traveling from a dense optical glass medium of refractive index n1 = 1.62 into a medium of refractive index n2 = 1.22.
A virtual image of an object is formed 10.0 cm in front of a thin concave lens of focal length 15.0 cm. Calculate the object distance u.
qs.e: Sign conventions for concave lens: focal length f = -15.0 cm, virtual image distance v = -10.0 cm. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v => -1/15 = 1/u - 1/10 => 1/u = 1/10 - 1/15 = (3 - 2)/30 = 1/30 => u = +30.0 cm.

qs.q: A 5.0 µF capacitor is charged through a 200 kΩ resistor by a 12 V DC source. Calculate the time constant (tau) of the RC charging circuit.
qs.e: Time constant τ = R × C = (200 × 10³ Ω) × (5.0 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 1.0 s.

qs.q: An experiment to determine internal resistance r and emf E of a cell yields two data points: V1 = 1.40 V when I1 = 0.20 A, and V2 = 1.20 V when I2 = 0.60 A. Calculate the emf E and internal resistance r.
A rectangular coil of 200 turns measuring 10 cm by 5 cm carries a current of 3.0 A in a uniform magnetic field of 0.50 T. Calculate the maximum torque exerted on the coil.
qs.e: Area A = 0.10 m × 0.05 m = 0.005 m². Maximum torque τ_max = N · B · I · A = 200 × 0.50 T × 3.0 A × 0.005 m² = 1.50 N·m.

qs.q: A series RLC circuit consists of a 10 Ω resistor, an inductor of L = 0.10 H, and a capacitor of C = 10 µF connected across a 100 V rms AC voltage source. Calculate the resonant angular frequency (omega_0) of the circuit.
Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an alpha particle (mass m = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, charge q = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 1.0 kV (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s).
A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 8.0 hours. Calculate the fraction of the initial activity remaining after a time interval of 20.0 hours.

In an ideal operational amplifier non-inverting configuration, R1 = 5.0 kΩ and feedback resistor R2 = 45.0 kΩ. If an input signal of 0.20 V is applied to the non-inverting input, calculate the output voltage V_out.
qs.e: Non-inverting op-amp voltage gain A_v = 1 + (R2 / R1) = 1 + (45.0 kΩ / 5.0 kΩ) = 1 + 9 = 10. Output voltage V_out = A_v × V_in = 10 × 0.20 V = +2.00 V.

qs.q: At what water depth in a calm lake will the total absolute pressure be equal to three times the normal atmospheric pressure at sea level? (P_atm = 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, density of fresh water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Total pressure P_total = P_atm + h·ρ·g = 3 · P_atm => h·ρ·g = 2 · P_atm => h × 1000 × 10 = 2 × 100,000 => 10,000 h = 200,000 => h = 20 m.

qs.q: A flywheel wheel of radius 0.25 m rotates about its central axis at 600 revolutions per minute (rpm). Calculate the linear tangential speed of a point on the outer rim of the wheel (take π = 3.142).
qs.e: Angular velocity ω = 600 × 2π / 60 = 20π rad/s = 20 × 3.1416 = 62.83 rad/s. Tangential speed v = ω · r = 62.83 rad/s × 0.25 m = 15.708 m/s ≈ 15.71 m/s.

qs.q: A block of mass 5.0 kg resting against a rough vertical wall is held at rest by applying a horizontal force F perpendicular to the wall. If coefficient of static friction µ_s = 0.40, calculate the minimum force F required (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Vertical balance: Maximum static friction f_s = µ_s · N = µ_s · F must balance weight W = m·g => 0.40 · F = 5.0 kg × 10 m/s² = 50 N => F = 50 / 0.40 = 125 N.

qs.q: A 2.0 kg mass moving at 8.0 m/s collides elastically with a stationary 6.0 kg mass on a smooth horizontal table. Calculate the final velocity of the 2.0 kg mass after impact.

A solar water heater panel of area 2.0 m² receives solar radiation at a rate of 800 W/m². If 60% of the incident radiation is converted into thermal power, calculate the rate of heat gain of the water.
qs.e: Total incident power = Area × Intensity = 2.0 m² × 800 W/m² = 1600 W. Useful thermal power = 0.60 × 1600 W = 960 W.

qs.q: According to the maximum power transfer theorem, a DC source of emf E and internal resistance r delivers maximum power to an external load resistor R when R is equal to:
qs.e: The Maximum Power Transfer Theorem states that maximum power is transferred from a source to a load when the load resistance R equals the source internal resistance r.

qs.q: A system consists of a block m1 = 4.0 kg on a 30° inclined plane connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley to a hanging mass m2 = 3.0 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between m1 and the plane is µ = 0.20. Calculate the acceleration of the system as m2 descends (g = 10 m/s², cos 30° = 0.866).
qs.e: Forces along incline on m1 (moving up): gravity component m1·g·sin(30°) = 4 × 10 × 0.5 = 20 N. Normal N = m1·g·cos(30°) = 4 × 10 × 0.866 = 34.64 N. Friction f_k = µ·N = 0.20 × 34.64 N = 6.93 N. Downward force on m2 = m2·g = 3.0 × 10 = 30 N. Net driving force F_net = m2·g - m1·g·sin(30°) - f_k = 30 N - 20 N - 6.93 N = 3.07 N. Total mass = 4.0 + 3.0 = 7.0 kg. Acceleration a = F_net / (m1 + m2) = 3.07 N / 7.0 kg = 0.4386 m/s² ≈ 0.44 m/s².

qs.q: A Carnot heat engine operating between a hot reservoir at 500 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K absorbs 1000 J of heat per cycle. The mechanical work output of this Carnot engine is used to drive a ideal Carnot refrigerator operating between 250 K and 300 K. Calculate the heat removed from the cold reservoir of the refrigerator per cycle.
qs.e: Carnot engine efficiency η = 1 - (Tc/Th) = 1 - (300/500) = 0.40 (40%). Work output W = η · Q_h = 0.40 × 1000 J = 400 J. Coefficient of performance (COP) of Carnot refrigerator = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 250 / (300 - 250) = 250 / 50 = 5.0. Heat removed Q_c_ref = COP × W = 5.0 × 400 J = 2000 J.

qs.q: A ray of light enters a glass prism (refractive index n = 1.50, apex angle A = 60°) at normal incidence on the first refracting face. Will the light ray undergo total internal reflection at the second face in air, and what is the critical angle of glass?
o: Yes, because angle of incidence 60° exceeds critical angle 41.8°
No, because angle of incidence 30° is less than critical angle 41.8°
No, light passes straight through without deviation
qs.e: At normal incidence on 1st face, angle of refraction r1 = 0°. Angle of incidence on 2nd face i2 = A - r1 = 60° - 0° = 60°. Critical angle for glass-air interface θ_c = sin⁻¹(1 / 1.50) = sin⁻¹(0.6667) = 41.81°. Since i2 (60°) > θ_c (41.81°), the ray undergoes total internal reflection at the 2nd face.

qs.q: A series RLC resonant circuit consists of an inductor L = 0.20 H, a capacitor C = 5.0 µF, and a resistor R = 10.0 Ω connected to a 220 V rms AC supply. Calculate the quality factor Q of the resonant circuit.
An electron is accelerated through a relativistic voltage of 1.02 MV (where rest mass energy m0·c² = 0.51 MeV). Calculate the relativistic mass of the electron in terms of its rest mass m0.
qs.e: Relativistic kinetic energy KE = (γ - 1)·m0·c² = 1.02 MeV. Given m0·c² = 0.51 MeV => (γ - 1) × 0.51 = 1.02 => γ - 1 = 2 => γ = 3. Relativistic mass m = γ·m0 = 3 m0.

qs.q: A radioactive parent nuclide A (half-life 10 hours) decays into a radioactive daughter nuclide B (half-life 100 hours), which decays into a stable isotope C. If a sample initially contains pure A, after a long period secular/transient equilibrium is established. Calculate the ratio of the number of nuclei N_B / N_A at equilibrium.
qs.e: In radioactive equilibrium, activity A_A ≈ activity A_B => λ_A · N_A = λ_B · N_B => N_B / N_A = λ_A / λ_B = T_half_B / T_half_A = 100 hours / 10 hours = 10.0.

qs.q: A uniform thin rigid rod of length L and mass M is pivoted smoothly at one end so it can swing freely as a physical pendulum in a vertical plane. Calculate the period T of small amplitude oscillations (moment of inertia about end I = ⅓·M·L²).
qs.e: Physical pendulum formula: T = 2π · √(I / (M·g·d_cm)). Distance from pivot to center of mass d_cm = L/2. Substituting I = ⅓·M·L²: T = 2π · √((⅓·M·L²) / (M·g·L/2)) = 2π · √(2L / 3g).

qs.q: A small bob of mass m suspended by a string of length L = 1.0 m rotates in a horizontal circle as a conical pendulum at an angle theta = 60° to the vertical. Calculate the tangential speed v of the bob (g = 10 m/s², sin 60° = 0.866, tan 60° = 1.732).
qs.e: Radius of circle r = L · sin θ = 1.0 m × 0.866 = 0.866 m. For conical pendulum, tan θ = v² / (r·g) => v = √(r · g · tan θ) = √(0.866 m × 10 m/s² × 1.732) = √(8.66 × 1.732) = √15.0 = 3.873 m/s ≈ 3.87 m/s.

qs.q: A small rubber ball dropped from a height H = 10.0 m onto a fixed steel floor rebounds repeatedly. If the coefficient of restitution between ball and floor is e = 0.80, calculate the total distance S travelled by the ball before coming to rest.

A solid uniform cylinder of radius R and mass M rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of height h = 3.0 m from rest. Calculate its linear speed at the bottom of the incline (g = 10 m/s², moment of inertia I = ½·M·R²).
qs.e: Conservation of energy: M·g·h = ½·M·v² + ½·I·ω² = ½·M·v² + ½(½·M·R²)(v/R)² = ½·M·v² + ¼·M·v² = ¾·M·v² => v = √(4gh / 3) = √(4 × 10 × 3.0 / 3) = √40 = 6.3245 m/s ≈ 6.32 m/s.

qs.q: A heavy uniform flexible cable of mass M = 10 kg and length L = 20 m hangs vertically from a rigid ceiling under its own weight. Calculate the total elastic energy stored in the hanging cable if cross-sectional area A = 1.0 cm² (1.0 × 10⁻⁴ m²) and Young's modulus E = 2.0 × 10¹¹ N/m² (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Tension at distance y from bottom T(y) = (M/L)·g·y. Energy element dW = [T(y)]² dy / (2·A·E) = (M² g² / (2 A E L²)) y² dy. Integrating from 0 to L: W = M² · g² · L / (6 · A · E) = (10² × 10² × 20) / (6 × 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ × 2.0 × 10¹¹) = 200,000 / (1.2 × 10⁸) = 0.001667 J? Wait! (100 × 100 × 20) = 200,000. 6 × 10⁻⁴ × 2 × 10¹¹ = 1.2 × 10⁸. 2e5 / 1.2e8 = 0.001667 J. Let's adjust L = 200 m or options to match!

qs.q: A open cylindrical water tank of radius R = 1.0 m has a small circular drainage orifice of radius r = 2.0 cm at its base. Using Torricelli's law, calculate the time required for the water level in the tank to drop from an initial height H1 = 4.0 m to H2 = 1.0 m (g = 10 m/s²).
A ship model floats in a naval testing basin. For stable floatation, the metacentric height M_G of a floating vessel must be:
o: Greater than zero (Metacenter M located above center of gravity G)
Equal to zero (Metacenter M coincides with G)
Less than zero (Metacenter M located below G)
Independent of center of buoyancy B
qs.e: A floating body is in stable equilibrium if its metacentric height GM is positive (metacenter M lies above the center of gravity G), producing a restoring righting moment when tilted.

qs.q: According to Poiseuille's law, the volumetric flow rate Q of a viscous liquid through a smooth horizontal capillary tube of radius r and length L under a pressure difference ΔP is proportional to:
qs.e: Poiseuille's formula Q = (π · r⁴ · ΔP) / (8 · η · L) shows that flow rate Q is directly proportional to r⁴ and ΔP, and inversely proportional to length L and viscosity η.

qs.q: An ideal diatomic gas (gamma = 1.40) at an initial pressure of 100 kPa and volume 5.0 L is compressed adiabatically to a volume of 1.0 L. Calculate the final pressure of the gas.
The mean free path lambda of gas molecules in an ideal gas container at absolute temperature T and pressure P is directly proportional to:
qs.e: Mean free path λ = 1 / (√2 · π · d² · n). Since number density n = N/V = P / (k_B · T), substituting gives λ = (k_B · T) / (√2 · π · d² · P) ∝ T / P.

qs.q: An acoustic pipe of length L = 0.85 m is closed at one end and open at the other. Taking end correction e = 0.6·r (where tube radius r = 2.5 cm) and sound speed v = 340 m/s, calculate the fundamental resonance frequency.
qs.e: Effective length L_eff = L + e = 0.85 m + (0.6 × 0.025 m) = 0.85 + 0.015 = 0.865 m. For pipe closed at one end, fundamental wavelength λ = 4 · L_eff = 4 × 0.865 m = 3.46 m. Fundamental frequency f0 = v / λ = 340 m/s / 3.46 m = 98.265 Hz ≈ 98.3 Hz.

qs.q: In a Newton's rings interference experiment, monochromatic light of wavelength λ = 589 nm illuminates a plano-convex lens of radius of curvature R = 2.0 m resting on a flat glass plate. Calculate the radius of the 10th dark interference ring.
qs.e: Formula for radius of m-th dark ring in Newton's rings: r_m = √(m · λ · R) = √(10 × 589 × 10⁻⁹ m × 2.0 m) = √(1.178 × 10⁻⁵) = √(11.78 × 10⁻⁶) = 3.432 × 10⁻³ m = 3.43 mm.

qs.q: Three point charges +q, +q, and -q are fixed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side length a in vacuum. Calculate the total electrostatic potential energy of the three-charge system (k = 1 / (4πε0)).
qs.e: Pairs: (1,2) with charges +q,+q at distance a => U12 = +k q²/a. (1,3) with charges +q,-q at distance a => U13 = -k q²/a. (2,3) with charges +q,-q at distance a => U23 = -k q²/a. Total energy U = U12 + U13 + U23 = (+k q²/a) - (k q²/a) - (k q²/a) = -k · q² / a.

qs.q: An infinite ladder network consists of repeating 1.0 Ω series resistors and 1.0 Ω parallel resistors connected to a DC source. Calculate the equivalent input resistance R_in across the terminals.
qs.e: Let input resistance be R. The infinite network after the first L-section has same input resistance R. Therefore, R = R_series + (R_parallel || R) = 1 + (1 · R)/(1 + R). R = 1 + R/(1 + R) => R(1 + R) = 1 + R + R => R + R² = 1 + 2R => R² - R - 1 = 0. Quadratic solution: R = (1 + √5)/2 = (1 + 2.236068)/2 = 1.618034 Ω ≈ 1.618 Ω (the golden ratio!).

qs.q: In a Hall effect measurement, a semiconductor strip of thickness t = 0.50 mm carrying a current I = 10.0 mA in a magnetic field B = 0.20 T develops a Hall voltage V_H = 2.5 mV. Calculate the charge carrier density n (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).

Two coaxial solenoids have mutual inductance M = 50 mH. If the electric current in the primary solenoid changes from +4.0 A to -4.0 A in a time interval of 0.020 seconds, calculate the magnitude of average induced emf in the secondary solenoid.
qs.e: Change in current ΔI = -4.0 - (+4.0) = -8.0 A. Rate of change dI/dt = -8.0 A / 0.020 s = -400 A/s. Induced emf E = -M · (dI/dt) = -(0.050 H) × (-400 A/s) = +20.0 V.

qs.q: In a Compton scattering experiment, an X-ray photon of initial wavelength λ = 0.0200 nm is scattered by a free electron through a scattering angle θ = 90°. Calculate the wavelength shift Δλ and the final scattered wavelength λ' (Compton wavelength h / (m_e·c) = 0.00243 nm).
qs.e: Compton shift formula: Δλ = (h / (m_e · c)) · (1 - cos θ) = 0.00243 nm × (1 - cos 90°) = 0.00243 nm × (1 - 0) = 0.00243 nm. Final scattered wavelength λ' = λ + Δλ = 0.0200 + 0.00243 = 0.02243 nm.

qs.q: An operational amplifier active integrator circuit has input resistor R = 100 kΩ and feedback capacitor C = 1.0 µF. If a constant DC voltage V_in = -2.0 V is applied at t = 0, calculate the rate of change of output voltage (dV_out / dt).
qs.e: Op-amp integrator equation: dV_out / dt = -V_in / (R · C) = -(-2.0 V) / (100 × 10³ Ω × 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ F) = +2.0 / 0.10 s = +20.0 V/s.

qs.q: In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, calculate the orbital radius r1 of the electron in the ground state (n = 1) given Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, m_e = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and permittivity of free space ε0 = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m.
An atom of potassium is represented as ³⁹₁₉K⁺. How many protons, neutrons, and electrons are present in this ion?
qs.e: The atomic number (Z) = 19, which is the number of protons. Mass number (A) = 39. Number of neutrons = A - Z = 39 - 19 = 20. Since it has a +1 charge, it has lost 1 electron: 19 - 1 = 18 electrons.

qs.q: What is the ground-state electronic configuration of an aluminum ion, Al³⁺ (atomic number = 13)?
qs.e: A neutral aluminum atom (Z=13) has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p¹. Upon forming the Al³⁺ cation, it loses its 3 valence electrons (3s² 3p¹), leaving 10 electrons with the stable configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶.

qs.q: In which period and group of the Periodic Table is an element with atomic number 16 located?
qs.e: An element with Z=16 (sulfur) has electronic configuration 2, 8, 6. It has 3 electron shells, placing it in Period 3. With 6 valence electrons, it belongs to Group 16 (or Group 6).

qs.q: Across Period 3 of the Periodic Table, from sodium to chlorine, the atomic radius generally decreases because of an increase in:
qs.e: Across a period, protons are added to the nucleus while electrons enter the same main energy level. The increased effective nuclear charge pulls the outer shell closer to the nucleus, decreasing atomic radius.

qs.q: Which of the following processes occurs during the formation of an ionic (electrovalent) bond between sodium and chlorine?
o: Complete transfer of one electron from sodium to chlorine
Equal sharing of an electron pair between sodium and chlorine
Dative donation of a lone pair from chlorine to sodium
Formation of a sea of delocalized valence electrons
qs.e: Ionic bonding occurs when a metal atom (Na) loses a valence electron to form Na⁺ and a non-metal atom (Cl) gains that electron to form Cl⁻, resulting in electrovalent attraction between opposite ions.

qs.q: How many single covalent bonds and lone pairs of electrons are present in a molecule of ammonia, NH₃?
o: 3 single covalent bonds and 0 lone pairs
3 single covalent bonds and 1 lone pair
2 single covalent bonds and 2 lone pairs
4 single covalent bonds and 0 lone pairs
qs.e: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons. It shares 3 single electrons with 3 hydrogen atoms to form 3 single covalent bonds, leaving 1 non-bonding pair (lone pair) of electrons on the central nitrogen atom.

qs.q: What is the mass of 0.20 moles of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Relative atomic masses: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40.0 g/mol. Mass = moles × molar mass = 0.20 mol × 40.0 g/mol = 8.0 g.

qs.q: How many molecules are contained in 0.25 moles of carbon dioxide gas, CO₂? (Avogadro's constant, N₇ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
qs.e: Number of molecules = moles × Avogadro's constant = 0.25 mol × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 1.505 × 10²³ molecules.

qs.q: In the balanced chemical equation 2Al(s) + 3Cl₂(g) → 2AlCl₃(s), what is the mole ratio of aluminum to chlorine gas?
qs.e: The stoichiometric coefficients in the balanced equation show that 2 moles of solid aluminum react with 3 moles of chlorine gas, giving a mole ratio of 2 : 3.

qs.q: The Law of Conservation of Mass states that in any chemical reaction in a closed system, the total mass of the reactants is:
o: Greater than the total mass of the products
Equal to the total mass of the products
Less than the total mass of the products
qs.e: The Law of Conservation of Mass dictates that matter is neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction, so total mass of reactants equals total mass of products.

qs.q: The direct change of a solid substance into its gaseous state upon heating without passing through the liquid phase is called:
qs.e: Sublimation is the phase transition directly from solid to gas without entering an intermediate liquid state, seen in substances like iodine, ammonium chloride, and dry ice.

qs.q: In which state of matter do particles possess the highest average kinetic energy and weakest intermolecular forces at a given temperature?
qs.e: Gas particles have high kinetic energy, moving rapidly and randomly with negligible intermolecular forces compared to liquids and solids.

qs.q: According to Boyle's law, for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, the pressure is:
o: Directly proportional to its absolute temperature
Inversely proportional to its absolute temperature
qs.e: Boyle's law states that P ∝ 1/V at constant temperature, meaning pressure and volume are inversely proportional (P₁V₁ = P₂V₂).

qs.q: What volume is occupied by 1.5 moles of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.)? (Molar volume of gas at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Volume = moles × molar volume = 1.5 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 33.6 dm³.

qs.q: A substance that absorbs moisture from the atmosphere and dissolves in it to form a solution is described as:
qs.e: Deliquescent substances (like NaOH, CaCl₂) absorb enough atmospheric water vapor to dissolve completely and form a concentrated liquid solution.

qs.q: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride paper changes color from blue to pink in the presence of:
qs.e: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue and turns pink upon hydration (forming CoCl₂·6H₂O), serving as a standard test for the presence of water.

qs.q: Powdered zinc reacts much faster with dilute hydrochloric acid than a zinc strip of equal mass because the powder has:
o: A greater surface area per unit mass
A greater concentration of zinc atoms
qs.e: Increasing the surface area increases the number of exposed particles available for collision per unit time, resulting in a higher frequency of effective collisions.

qs.q: A chemical substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed at the end of the reaction is a:
qs.e: A positive catalyst accelerates a chemical reaction by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy while remaining chemically unchanged overall.

qs.q: A dynamic chemical equilibrium is established in a reversible reaction when:
o: The concentrations of reactants and products become equal
All chemical reactions in the system come to a complete stop
The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
The total mass of products exceeds the mass of reactants
qs.e: Dynamic equilibrium occurs when forward and backward reactions proceed at equal rates, keeping reactant and product concentrations constant over time.

qs.q: What is the effect of adding a catalyst to a chemical reaction already at dynamic equilibrium?
o: It shifts the equilibrium position toward the products
It increases the equilibrium constant, K_c
It shifts the equilibrium position toward the reactants
It speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally without shifting the equilibrium position
qs.e: A catalyst lowers activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions by the same amount, helping reach equilibrium faster without altering the equilibrium position or K_c.

qs.q: An exothermic reaction is characterized by which of the following energy changes?
o: Heat is released to the surroundings, and ΔH is negative
Heat is absorbed from the surroundings, and ΔH is positive
Heat is released to the surroundings, and ΔH is positive
No heat exchange occurs with the surroundings, and ΔH is zero
qs.e: In exothermic reactions, energy is liberated to the surroundings as products have lower enthalpy than reactants, giving a negative enthalpy change (ΔH < 0).

qs.q: The standard enthalpy of combustion of a substance is defined as the heat change when:
o: 1 mole of the substance is formed from its constituent elements
1 mole of the substance burns completely in excess oxygen under standard conditions
1 mole of water is produced during an acid-base neutralization
1 mole of bonds in the substance is broken in the gas phase
qs.e: Standard heat of combustion is the energy released when 1 mole of a compound undergoes complete combustion in oxygen under standard conditions (298 K, 1 atm).

qs.q: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid is defined as a:
o: Substance that produces hydroxide ions in water
qs.e: Brønsted-Lowry theory defines an acid as a species that donates a proton (H⁺ ion) and a base as a proton acceptor.

qs.q: What is the pH of a 0.001 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid (HCl) solution, assuming complete dissociation?
qs.e: HCl is a strong monoprotic acid, so [H⁺] = 0.001 M = 10⁻³ M. pH = -log₁₀[H⁺] = -log₁₀(10⁻³) = 3.0.

qs.q: Which of the following salts dissolves in water to give an alkaline (basic) solution?
qs.e: Sodium ethanoate is a salt formed from a weak acid (CH₃COOH) and a strong base (NaOH). The ethanoate ion hydrolyzes in water: CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻, giving a basic solution.

qs.q: Which of the following salt types is formed when all replaceable hydrogen ions in an acid are completely replaced by metallic or ammonium ions?
qs.e: A normal salt (e.g., Na₂SO₄, NaCl) results when all acidic hydrogen atoms of an acid are replaced by metal cations or ammonium ions.

qs.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in potassium permanganate, KMnO₄?
qs.e: In KMnO₄: K = +1, O = -2 (4 × -2 = -8). Sum of oxidation numbers = 0: (+1) + Mn + (-8) = 0 → Mn = +7.

qs.q: In the displacement reaction Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s), zinc acts as:
o: An oxidizing agent because it gains electrons
A reducing agent because it gains electrons
An oxidizing agent because it loses electrons
A reducing agent because it loses electrons
qs.e: Zinc atom loses 2 electrons to become Zn²⁺ (oxidation). By donating electrons to Cu²⁺, zinc acts as the reducing agent.

qs.q: During the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride using inert graphite electrodes, the product formed at the cathode is:
qs.e: In molten NaCl, Na⁺ ions migrate to the negative electrode (cathode) where they gain electrons (reduction) to form sodium metal: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na.

qs.q: The quantity of electric charge carried by one mole of electrons is known as Faraday's constant and is approximately equal to:
In a standard voltaic (galvanic) cell, oxidation always takes place at the:
o: Cathode, which is the negative electrode
Anode, which is the positive electrode
Anode, which is the negative electrode
Cathode, which is the positive electrode
qs.e: Anode is defined as the electrode where oxidation occurs. In a galvanic cell, oxidation releases electrons at the anode, making it negative.

qs.q: What is the general molecular formula for aliphatic straight-chain alkenes containing one carbon-carbon double bond?
qs.e: Alkenes with one double bond have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ (e.g., ethene C₂H₄, propene C₃H₆).

qs.q: Which functional group characterizes the organic homologous series of alkanols (alcohols)?
qs.e: Alkanols contain the hydroxyl (-OH) functional group bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

qs.q: Polyethene is a synthetic polymer formed by the addition polymerization of which monomer?
qs.e: Polyethene is produced by double bond opening and joining of ethene monomer units (CH₂=CH₂).

qs.q: Which atmospheric gaseous pollutant is primarily responsible for the formation of acid rain?
qs.e: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in atmospheric water droplets to form sulfurous and sulfuric acids, leading to acid rain.

qs.q: Naturally occurring chlorine consists of two isotopes: ³⁵Cl (75.0% abundance) and ³⁷Cl (25.0% abundance). Calculate the relative atomic mass of chlorine.
An element X has two main isotopes, ¹⁰X and ¹¹X. If its relative atomic mass is 10.8, what is the percentage abundance of the ¹¹X isotope?
qs.e: Let y be the percentage of ¹¹X. Then (100 - y) is the percentage of ¹⁰X. RAM = [11y + 10(100 - y)] / 100 = 10.8 → 11y + 1000 - 10y = 1080 → y = 80.0%.

qs.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy the third principal energy level (n = 3) of an atom?
qs.e: The maximum electron capacity of a principal shell is given by 2n². For n = 3: 2 × 3² = 2 × 9 = 18 electrons (2 in 3s, 6 in 3p, 10 in 3d).

qs.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in the ground-state electron configuration of a neutral nitrogen atom (atomic number = 7)?
qs.e: Nitrogen (Z=7) has configuration 1s² 2s² 2p³. According to Hund's rule, the 3 p-orbitals each receive one electron with parallel spins, giving 3 unpaired electrons.

qs.q: The first ionization energy of magnesium (1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s²) is higher than that of aluminum (1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p¹) because:
o: Aluminum has a smaller atomic radius than magnesium
Magnesium has a lower nuclear charge than aluminum
Aluminum has more inner shielding shells than magnesium
Magnesium has a stable, fully filled 3s subshell
qs.e: Removing an electron from aluminum involves a single 3p electron, which is higher in energy and shielded by 3s, whereas magnesium has a completely filled, stable 3s² subshell.

qs.q: Which oxide of Period 3 elements displays amphoteric properties, reacting with both strong acids and strong bases?
qs.e: Aluminum oxide Al₂O₃ is amphoteric: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O and Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH + 3H₂O → 2Na[Al(OH)₄].

qs.q: Arrange the following isoelectronic ions in order of decreasing ionic radius: N³⁻, O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺.
qs.e: All four ions have 10 electrons. As nuclear charge increases from N (Z=7) to Na (Z=11), nuclear pull on electrons increases, making Na⁺ smallest and N³⁻ largest.

qs.q: A coordinate (dative covalent) bond is formed in the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺, when a molecule of ammonia donates an electron pair to:
qs.e: Ammonia has a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen, which is donated to an electron-deficient H⁺ ion (having an empty 1s orbital) to form NH₄⁺.

qs.q: Why is carbon tetrachloride, CCl₄, a non-polar molecule despite containing four polar C-Cl covalent bonds?
o: The electronegativity difference between C and Cl is zero
It forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds
The chlorine atoms share electrons completely equally with carbon
Its symmetrical tetrahedral geometry causes the bond dipoles to cancel out
qs.e: CCl₄ has a symmetrical tetrahedral arrangement. The dipoles of the four polar C-Cl bonds point in opposite directions and vectorially cancel out, giving zero net dipole moment.

qs.q: The significantly higher boiling point of ethanol (78.5 °C) compared to its structural isomer dimethyl ether (-24.0 °C) is attributed to:
qs.e: Ethanol contains an -OH group capable of forming intermolecular hydrogen bonds, requiring additional energy to break during boiling, whereas dimethyl ether cannot form H-bonds.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of 4.48 dm³ of carbon dioxide gas, CO₂, measured at s.t.p. (Molar mass of CO₂ = 44.0 g/mol; Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Moles of CO₂ = 4.48 dm³ / 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.20 mol. Mass = 0.20 mol × 44.0 g/mol = 8.8 g.

qs.q: How many total hydrogen atoms are contained in 0.50 moles of methane gas, CH₄? (Avogadro's constant = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
qs.e: 1 mole of CH₄ contains 4 moles of H atoms. Total H atoms = 0.50 mol × 4 × (6.02 × 10²³) = 2.0 mol H atoms = 1.204 × 10²⁴ atoms.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in urea, CO(NH₂)₂. (Relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16, N = 14, H = 1)
What mass of calcium oxide, CaO, is produced by the complete thermal decomposition of 25.0 g of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
qs.e: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g). Molar masses: CaCO₃ = 100 g/mol, CaO = 56 g/mol. Moles of CaCO₃ = 25.0 / 100 = 0.25 mol. Mass CaO = 0.25 mol × 56 g/mol = 14.0 g.

qs.q: What volume of oxygen gas at s.t.p. is required for the complete combustion of 5.6 dm³ of methane gas, CH₄? CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)
qs.e: By Gay-Lussac's Law, gas volumes at the same T and P react in simple whole-number ratios. 1 vol CH₄ requires 2 vols O₂. Volume of O₂ = 2 × 5.6 dm³ = 11.2 dm³.

qs.q: Under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, compare the rate of diffusion of methane, CH₄ (molar mass = 16) with sulfur dioxide, SO₂ (molar mass = 64). Methane diffuses:
o: 4.0 times as fast as sulfur dioxide
0.5 times as fast as sulfur dioxide
2.0 times as fast as sulfur dioxide
1.41 times as fast as sulfur dioxide
qs.e: By Graham's Law, rate₁/rate₂ = √(M₂/M₁). Rate(CH₄)/Rate(SO₂) = √(64 / 16) = √4 = 2.0. Methane diffuses twice as fast.

qs.q: The vapor pressure of a liquid in a closed container increases when:
o: The volume of the liquid is doubled at constant temperature
The surface area of the liquid is decreased
The temperature of the liquid is raised
qs.e: Vapor pressure depends strictly on temperature for a given liquid. Increasing temperature increases kinetic energy, enabling more molecules to escape into the vapor phase.

qs.q: A fixed mass of gas occupies 500 cm³ at 27 °C. What volume will it occupy at 127 °C if the pressure remains constant?
qs.e: Charles's Law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. Temperatures in Kelvin: T₁ = 27 + 273 = 300 K, T₂ = 127 + 273 = 400 K. V₂ = 500 × (400 / 300) = 666.7 cm³.

qs.q: A sample of gas has a pressure of 2.0 atm and a volume of 4.0 L at 300 K. If compressed to 2.0 L and heated to 450 K, what is its new pressure?
qs.e: Combined Gas Law: (P₁V₁)/T₁ = (P₂V₂)/T₂. P₂ = (P₁V₁T₂) / (V₂T₁) = (2.0 × 4.0 × 450) / (2.0 × 300) = 3600 / 600 = 6.0 atm.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage mass of water in hydrated zinc sulfate, ZnSO₄·7H₂O. (Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
When a 5.00 g sample of hydrated salt is heated to constant mass, 3.20 g of anhydrous residue remains. What is the percentage of water of crystallization?
qs.e: Mass of water lost = 5.00 g - 3.20 g = 1.80 g. Percentage water = (1.80 / 5.00) × 100 = 36.0%.

qs.q: If 0.040 moles of carbon dioxide gas are produced during the first 20 seconds of a reaction, what is the average rate of reaction in mol/s?
qs.e: Average rate = Δquantity / Δtime = 0.040 mol / 20 s = 0.0020 mol/s.

qs.q: Adding manganese(IV) oxide (MnO₂) to a solution of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) accelerates its decomposition because MnO₂:
o: Increases the total enthalpy of the reaction
Provides an alternative reaction mechanism with a lower activation energy
Increases the kinetic energy of hydrogen peroxide molecules
Consumes the water produced to drive the reaction forward
qs.e: MnO₂ functions as a positive catalyst, providing a lower activation energy pathway without affecting the overall enthalpy change or thermal energy of reactant molecules.

qs.q: Write the equilibrium constant expression (K_c) for the gas-phase reaction: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g).
qs.e: For a general equilibrium aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, K_c = ([C]^c [D]^d) / ([A]^a [B]^b). Here K_c = [SO₃]² / ([SO₂]² [O₂]).

qs.q: For the industrial Haber reaction: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH = -92 kJ/mol. How will an increase in temperature affect the equilibrium mixture?
o: Shift the equilibrium to the right, increasing the yield of ammonia
Have no effect on the equilibrium yield of ammonia
Shift the equilibrium to the left, decreasing the yield of ammonia
qs.e: By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature favors the endothermic direction (reverse reaction here) to absorb heat, shifting equilibrium left and lowering NH₃ yield.

qs.q: Calculate the amount of heat energy absorbed when 100 g of water is heated from 25 °C to 40 °C. (Specific heat capacity of water = 4.18 J/g·K)
Given the thermochemical equation H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l), ΔH = -285.8 kJ/mol, how much heat is liberated when 3.60 g of liquid water is formed?
qs.e: Molar mass of H₂O = 18.0 g/mol. Moles formed = 3.60 / 18.0 = 0.20 mol. Heat released = 0.20 mol × 285.8 kJ/mol = 57.16 kJ.

qs.q: What is the pH of a 0.005 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) solution, assuming sulfuric acid undergoes complete dissociation into ions?
qs.e: H₂SO₄ → 2H⁺ + SO₄²⁻. [H⁺] = 2 × 0.005 mol/dm³ = 0.010 mol/dm³ = 10⁻² M. pH = -log₁₀(10⁻²) = 2.0.

qs.q: What concentration of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution is required if 25.0 cm³ of it neutralizes exactly 20.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ acid?
Identify the conjugate base of the hydrogen sulfate ion, HSO₄⁻, according to Brønsted-Lowry acid-base theory.
qs.e: A conjugate base is formed when an acid donates a proton. Removing H⁺ from HSO₄⁻ leaves SO₄²⁻.

qs.q: Which of the following methods is most suitable for preparing an insoluble salt such as lead(II) sulfate, PbSO₄?
o: Titration of acid with soluble base
Action of acid on insoluble metal oxide
qs.e: Insoluble salts are prepared by precipitation (double decomposition) by mixing solutions containing the constituent aqueous ions, e.g., Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + Na₂SO₄(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2NaNO₃(aq).

qs.q: A hydrated salt that spontaneously loses its water of crystallization when exposed to dry air is termed:
qs.e: Efflorescence occurs when the vapor pressure of the hydrated salt exceeds the partial pressure of water vapor in surrounding air, causing loss of water of crystallization (e.g., Na₂CO₃·10H₂O).

qs.q: What is the oxidation state of chromium in potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇?
In the redox reaction 2H₂S(g) + SO₂(g) → 3S(s) + 2H₂O(l), sulfur dioxide (SO₂) functions as:
o: An oxidizing agent because it gains electrons
A reducing agent because it loses electrons
A catalyst because it speeds up the reaction
Neither an oxidizing nor reducing agent
qs.e: In SO₂, sulfur has an oxidation number of +4, which drops to 0 in S(s) (reduction). SO₂ acts as the oxidizing agent by accepting electrons from H₂S.

qs.q: What mass of copper (atomic mass = 64 g/mol) is deposited at the cathode when a constant current of 2.0 A is passed through aqueous CuSO₄ for 1930 seconds? (1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
During the electrolysis of dilute H₂SO₄, what volume of oxygen gas (at s.t.p.) is evolved at the anode when a current of 1.0 A passes for 3860 seconds?
Calculate the standard cell potential (E°_cell) for the galvanic cell Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s), given standard reduction potentials: E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = -0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V.
qs.e: E°_cell = E°_cathode - E°_anode = E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) - E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = +0.34 V - (-0.76 V) = +1.10 V.

qs.q: In a standard Daniel cell (Zn-Cu cell), in which direction do electrons flow in the external circuit?
o: From the zinc electrode (anode) to the copper electrode (cathode)
From the copper electrode to the zinc electrode
From the salt bridge into the zinc electrode
From the electrolyte to the external wire
qs.e: Zinc undergoes oxidation at the anode (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻), releasing electrons that travel through the external wire to the copper cathode where reduction occurs.

qs.q: How many structural isomer acyclic alkanes exist with the molecular formula C₅H₁₂?
qs.e: C₅H₁₂ has 3 structural isomers: pentane (n-pentane), 2-methylbutane (isopentane), and 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane).

qs.q: The major organic product formed when propene reacts with hydrogen bromide (HBr) is 2-bromopropane rather than 1-bromopropane according to:
qs.e: Markovnikov's rule states that in electrophilic addition to an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen atom attaches to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms, forming 2-bromopropane.

qs.q: Primary alkanols are oxidized by acidified potassium dichromate(VI) upon mild heating with immediate distillation to produce:
qs.e: Controlled oxidation of a primary alcohol with immediate distillation prevents further oxidation to carboxyl acid, yielding an alkanal (aldehyde).

qs.q: Esterification is a reversible reaction between an alkanoic acid and an alkanol in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ catalyst to yield:
qs.e: RCOOH + R'OH ⇌ RCOOR' + H₂O. Concentrated H₂SO₄ serves both as a catalyst and a dehydrating agent to shift equilibrium toward the ester.

qs.q: Tollen's reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate solution) is used to distinguish between alkanals and alkanones because alkanals:
o: Oxidize Tollen's reagent to produce a blue solution
Reduce Tollen's reagent to form a bright silver mirror
Decolorize Tollen's reagent without forming a precipitate
Form a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide
qs.e: Alkanals (aldehydes) are easily oxidized and reduce Ag⁺ in Tollen's reagent to metallic silver (silver mirror), whereas alkanones (ketones) are resistant to oxidation.

qs.q: The natural polymer rubber is a polyisotope macromolecule whose principal monomer building block is:
qs.e: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene, formed by polymerization of the monomer isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene).

qs.q: Nylon-6,6 is a synthetic polyamide produced by a condensation reaction between which two monomeric compounds?
qs.e: Nylon-6,6 is formed by condensation of adipic acid (hexane-1,6-dioic acid) and hexamethylenediamine (hexane-1,6-diamine), eliminating water molecules.

qs.q: In the extraction of iron in a blast furnace, limestone (CaCO₃) is added to the charge primarily to:
o: Remove silica (SiO₂) impurities by forming molten slag (CaSiO₃)
Reduce hematite (Fe₂O₃) directly to metallic iron
Act as a fuel to increase furnace temperature
Prevent oxidation of molten iron by air
qs.e: Limestone decomposes to CaO + CO₂. Quicklime (CaO) reacts with acidic silica impurities (SiO₂) to form liquid slag (CaSiO₃), which floats on molten iron.

qs.q: Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to purified alumina (Al₂O₃) during the industrial extraction of aluminum by the Hall-Héroult process to:
o: Prevent the carbon anodes from oxidizing to carbon dioxide
Lower the melting point of alumina from ~2050 °C to ~950 °C and increase electrical conductivity
Act as a reducing agent to convert Al³⁺ ions to aluminum metal
Precipitate impurities such as iron and silicon oxides
qs.e: Pure Al₂O₃ has a very high melting point (~2050 °C). Dissolving it in molten cryolite lowers the operating temperature to ~950 °C, reducing energy costs and increasing conductivity.

qs.q: The Ostwald process for the industrial manufacture of nitric acid involves the catalytic oxidation of ammonia over:
o: Iron catalyst with alumina promoter at 450 °C
qs.e: The first step of the Ostwald process oxidizes ammonia to nitrogen monoxide: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O using a platinum-rhodium gauze catalyst at 800–900 °C.

qs.q: Graphite conducts electricity along its crystal layers whereas diamond is an electrical insulator because graphite contains:
o: Free mobile ions within its macromolecular crystal
Weak van der Waals forces between its carbon atoms
sp³ hybridized carbon atoms with vacant d-orbitals
Delocalized pi-electrons from sp² hybridized carbon atoms
qs.e: In graphite, each carbon atom is sp² hybridized, forming 3 covalent bonds in planar hexagonal sheets. The fourth valence electron is delocalized over the sheet and carries current.

qs.q: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) released into the atmosphere contribute to stratospheric ozone depletion primarily because they release:
o: Chlorine free radicals under ultraviolet radiation
Fluoride ions that react with ozone molecules
Carbon monoxide gas that consumes oxygen
Nitrate radicals that decompose water vapor
qs.e: UV radiation breaks C-Cl bonds in CFCs to release reactive Cl• radicals, which catalytically decompose ozone: Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂.

qs.q: Industrial fractional distillation of liquefied air separates atmospheric nitrogen, oxygen, and argon based on differences in their:
qs.e: Liquefied air is warmed in a fractionating column. Nitrogen (b.p. -196 °C), argon (-186 °C), and oxygen (-183 °C) boil off at different temperatures.

qs.q: Which chemical reagent can be used to distinguish ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) from ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) by producing effervescence of a colorless gas?
qs.e: Ethanoic acid reacts with Na₂CO₃ to liberate CO₂ gas with effervescence: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑. Ethanol does not react with Na₂CO₃.

qs.q: In qualitative analysis, testing an aqueous solution with dilute nitric acid followed by silver nitrate solution gives a white precipitate that dissolves in dilute aqueous ammonia. This confirms the presence of:
qs.e: Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s) (white ppt). AgCl dissolves in dilute NH₃(aq) to form the soluble complex [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺.

qs.q: Which of the following drying agents is most suitable for drying alkaline ammonia gas, NH₃?
qs.e: Ammonia is basic and reacts with acidic drying agents (H₂SO₄, P₄O₁₀) and forms a complex with CaCl₂. Basic CaO (quicklime) does not react with NH₃.

qs.q: A photon of electromagnetic radiation emitted during an atomic electron transition has an energy of 3.31 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. What is the frequency of this radiation? (Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)
The water molecule, H₂O, adopts a bent (V-shaped) molecular geometry rather than a linear arrangement because of the presence of:
o: Three bonding pairs and one lone pair of electrons on oxygen
Four single covalent bonds arranged tetrahedrally
Two bonding pairs and two lone pairs of electrons on the central oxygen atom
Strong hydrogen bonds within the molecule
qs.e: Oxygen has 4 electron pairs (2 bonding, 2 lone pairs) arranged tetrahedrally. Lone pair-lone pair repulsion compresses the H-O-H bond angle to ~104.5°, giving a bent shape.

qs.q: What volume of 0.50 mol/dm³ HCl is required to neutralize 25.0 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ Na₂CO₃ solution? Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂
For a reaction A → Products, doubling the initial concentration of reactant A quadruples the initial reaction rate. What is the order of reaction with respect to A?
qs.e: Rate = k[A]^n. If concentration is doubled (2×) and rate quadruples (4×), 2^n = 4 → n = 2. The reaction is second order.

qs.q: Reductive ozonolysis of symmetrical alkene 2-butene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) yields which organic carbonyl product?
qs.e: Ozonolysis breaks the double bond of 2-butene: CH₃CH=CHCH₃ + O₃ → 2 CH₃CHO (two molecules of ethanal).

qs.q: Which gas is liberated when concentrated sulfuric acid is added to solid sodium chloride crystals in a dry test tube?
qs.e: NaCl(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄(s) + HCl(g)↑. Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as an acid displacing the volatile HCl gas from its salt.

qs.q: The diagram above illustrates the volume of hydrogen gas evolved against time for the reaction of excess zinc granules with 50 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ HCl (represented by Curve Y). Which of the following changes would produce Curve X?
o: Running the reaction at a lower temperature
Diluting the hydrochloric acid to 0.5 mol/dm³ with water
Using larger zinc chips while maintaining the same mass and concentration
Using the same mass of zinc powder instead of zinc granules
qs.e: Curve X shows a steeper initial slope, indicating a faster rate of reaction, but reaches the same final volume of gas. Using zinc powder instead of granules increases surface area, increasing the reaction rate without changing the moles of HCl, which limits the gas yield.

qs.q: An organic compound is analyzed and found to contain 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass. Determine its empirical formula. (Relative atomic masses: C = 12.0, H = 1.0)
qs.e: Moles of C = 85.7 / 12.0 = 7.14 mol. Moles of H = 14.3 / 1.0 = 14.3 mol. Divide by smallest: C = 7.14 / 7.14 = 1, H = 14.3 / 7.14 ≈ 2. The empirical formula is CH₂.

qs.q: An oxide of phosphorus contains 43.6% phosphorus and 56.4% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? (RAM: P = 31.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Moles of P = 43.6 / 31.0 = 1.406. Moles of O = 56.4 / 16.0 = 3.525. Divide by smallest: P = 1.406 / 1.406 = 1, O = 3.525 / 1.406 = 2.50. Multiply by 2 to get integers: P₂O₅.

qs.q: A mixture of 10.0 g of hydrogen gas and 32.0 g of oxygen gas is ignited in a closed vessel to form water vapor. What is the maximum mass of water produced? (H = 1.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Moles H₂ = 10.0 / 2.0 = 5.0 mol. Moles O₂ = 32.0 / 32.0 = 1.0 mol. Since 1 mol O₂ reacts with 2 mol H₂, O₂ is the limiting reactant. Maximum H₂O formed = 2.0 mol × 18.0 g/mol = 36.0 g.

qs.q: When 10.00 g of hydrated magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄·xH₂O) is heated to constant mass, 4.88 g of anhydrous residue is left. Determine the value of x. (Mg = 24.3, S = 32.1, O = 16.0, H = 1.0)
qs.e: Mass of water lost = 10.00 - 4.88 = 5.12 g. Molar mass of MgSO₄ = 24.3 + 32.1 + 64.0 = 120.4 g/mol. Moles of MgSO₄ = 4.88 / 120.4 = 0.0405 mol. Moles of H₂O = 5.12 / 18.0 = 0.2844 mol. x = 0.2844 / 0.0405 ≈ 7. The formula is MgSO₄·7H₂O.

qs.q: The density of a certain gas at standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.) is 1.43 g/dm³. What is the relative molecular mass of the gas? (Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Molar mass = Density × Molar volume = 1.43 g/dm³ × 22.4 dm³/mol = 32.03 g/mol ≈ 32.0 g/mol (which corresponds to oxygen gas, O₂).

qs.q: In a laboratory experiment using the Dumas method, 0.35 g of a volatile liquid produces 112 cm³ of vapor when measured at s.t.p. Calculate the molar mass of the liquid.
qs.e: Moles of vapor = 112 cm³ / 22,400 cm³/mol = 0.0050 mol. Molar mass = mass / moles = 0.35 g / 0.0050 mol = 70.0 g/mol.

qs.q: For the reversible reaction A(aq) + B(aq) ⇌ C(aq) + D(aq) conducted in a 1.0 dm³ vessel, the initial concentrations of A and B are both 1.0 mol/dm³. If 0.60 mol/dm³ of C is present at equilibrium, calculate the equilibrium constant, K_c.
Calculate the standard enthalpy of reaction (ΔH) for: C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g), given: C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = -393.5 kJ and CO(g) + ½O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = -283.0 kJ.
qs.e: According to Hess's Law, we subtract the second equation from the first: C(s) + O₂(g) - [CO(g) + ½O₂(g)] → CO₂(g) - CO₂(g) → C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g). ΔH = -393.5 kJ - (-283.0 kJ) = -110.5 kJ.

qs.q: A 0.50 g sample of impure calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is completely dissolved in 50.0 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ HCl. The excess acid requires 15.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ NaOH for complete neutralization. Calculate the percentage purity of the CaCO₃. (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
qs.e: Total moles of HCl added = 0.050 dm³ × 0.20 M = 0.0100 mol. Moles of NaOH used to neutralize excess acid = 0.015 dm³ × 0.10 M = 0.0015 mol. Moles of HCl reacting with CaCO₃ = 0.0100 - 0.0015 = 0.0085 mol. CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Moles of pure CaCO₃ = 0.0085 / 2 = 0.00425 mol. Mass of pure CaCO₃ = 0.00425 × 100 g/mol = 0.425 g. % purity = (0.425 / 0.50) × 100 = 85.0%.

qs.q: Two electrolytic cells containing aqueous AgNO₃ and CuSO₄ solutions are connected in series. If 2.16 g of silver is deposited in the first cell, calculate the mass of copper deposited in the second cell. (Ag = 108, Cu = 64, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Moles of Ag deposited = 2.16 / 108 = 0.020 mol, requiring 0.020 mol e⁻. In series, same current passes, so 0.020 mol e⁻ deposits 0.020 / 2 = 0.010 mol Cu. Mass Cu = 0.010 × 64 = 0.64 g.

qs.q: The complete combustion of 0.10 moles of a gaseous hydrocarbon yields 0.30 moles of carbon dioxide gas and 0.40 moles of water vapor. What is the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon?
qs.e: 0.10 mol of C_xH_y gives 0.30 mol CO₂ (0.30 mol C atoms) and 0.40 mol H₂O (0.80 mol H atoms). Therefore, 1 mole of hydrocarbon contains 3 moles of C atoms and 8 moles of H atoms, yielding C₃H₈.

qs.q: An organic liquid X with molecular formula C₂H₆O reacts with sodium metal to liberate a highly flammable gas, and reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid to yield a sweet-smelling compound. Compound X is:
qs.e: C₂H₆O can be ethanol (alcohol) or dimethyl ether. Reacting with sodium metal to produce hydrogen gas (2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂↑) and undergoing esterification identifies X as ethanol, an alkanol.

qs.q: In the industrial synthetic pathway Ethene → Ethanol → Ethanoic acid, what are the primary reagents and catalysts required for Step 1 and Step 2 respectively?
o: Step 1: Steam and H₃PO₄ catalyst at high temperature; Step 2: Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ and heat
Step 1: Hydrogen gas and Ni catalyst; Step 2: Sodium hydroxide solution
Step 1: Dilute HCl and heat; Step 2: Oxygen gas with Pt catalyst
Step 1: Water with yeast fermentation; Step 2: Concentrated sulfuric acid
qs.e: Step 1 is the catalytic hydration of ethene to ethanol using steam and H₃PO₄ catalyst. Step 2 is the chemical oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid using acidified potassium dichromate(VI) under heat.

qs.q: In the Down's cell for the extraction of sodium by the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, calcium chloride (CaCl₂) is added to the electrolyte to:
o: Prevent the newly formed sodium metal from dissolving in the melt
Lower the melting point of sodium chloride from 801 °C to about 600 °C
Increase the ionization of sodium chloride in the electrolytic bath
React with the liberated chlorine gas to form a non-toxic compound
qs.e: Adding CaCl₂ to NaCl creates a eutectic mixture, lowering the required temperature from 801 °C to ~600 °C, reducing energy consumption and preventing sodium vapor from escaping.

qs.q: What are the optimum temperature, pressure, and catalyst used in the converter of the Contact process for the catalytic oxidation of sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide? 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = -197 kJ/mol
qs.e: The conversion of SO₂ to SO₃ is exothermic. An optimum temperature of 450 °C gives a reasonable rate and yield. High pressure is unnecessary as yield is high at 1-2 atm over V₂O₅ catalyst.

qs.q: During qualitative analysis, adding a few drops of aqueous ammonia to a solution produces a pale blue precipitate that dissolves in excess ammonia to form a deep blue solution. This indicates the presence of:
qs.e: Cu²⁺ reacts with NH₃ to form Cu(OH)₂ (blue ppt), which dissolves in excess NH₃ to form the soluble tetraamminecopper(II) complex, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ (deep blue solution).

qs.q: Which cation forms a white gelatinous precipitate with sodium hydroxide solution that is soluble in excess sodium hydroxide, and also forms a white precipitate with aqueous ammonia that dissolves in excess ammonia?
qs.e: Both Zn²⁺ and Al³⁺ form white amphoteric hydroxides soluble in excess NaOH. Only Zn²⁺ forms a white hydroxide (Zn(OH)₂) soluble in excess NH₃ due to the formation of soluble tetraamminezinc, [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺.

qs.q: The 'brown ring' test, which involves adding freshly prepared iron(II) sulfate solution to a sample followed by slow addition of concentrated sulfuric acid down the side of the tube, is used to confirm the presence of:
qs.e: The brown ring is caused by the formation of the nitrosyliron(II) complex, [Fe(H₂O)₅(NO)]²⁺, at the junction of the two liquid layers, confirming the presence of NO₃⁻ ions.

qs.q: According to the Bohr model of the atom, calculate the energy of the photon emitted when an electron drops from energy level n = 3 (E₃ = -1.51 eV) to energy level n = 2 (E₂ = -3.40 eV).
qs.e: The energy of the emitted photon equals the difference in energy levels: ΔE = E₃ - E₂ = -1.51 eV - (-3.40 eV) = 1.89 eV.

qs.q: Describe the general trends in electronegativity across a period from left to right, and down a group from top to bottom, in the Periodic Table.
o: Decreases across a period, increases down a group
Increases across a period, increases down a group
Decreases across a period, decreases down a group
Increases across a period, decreases down a group
qs.e: Across a period, nuclear charge increases and atomic size decreases, attracting bonding electrons more strongly. Down a group, atomic size increases and shielding increases, decreasing electronegativity.

qs.q: What is the hybridization of the carbon orbitals in ethene, C₂H₄, and what is the resulting H-C-H bond angle?
qs.e: Each carbon in ethene is sp² hybridized, forming 3 sigma bonds (trigonal planar geometry, ~120° bond angle) and 1 pi bond through unhybridized 2p orbitals.

qs.q: What is the molecular geometry and the F-S-F bond angle of sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆?
qs.e: SF₆ has 6 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs of electrons on sulfur, adopting an octahedral geometry with equivalent F-S-F bond angles of 90°.

qs.q: Calculate the total number of ions present in 14.2 g of anhydrous sodium sulfate, Na₂SO₄. (Na = 23, S = 32, O = 16, Avogadro's constant = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
qs.e: Molar mass of Na₂SO₄ = 2(23) + 32 + 4(16) = 142 g/mol. Moles = 14.2 / 142 = 0.10 mol. Since Na₂SO₄ dissociates into 3 ions (2Na⁺ + SO₄²⁻), total ions = 0.10 × 3 × (6.02 × 10²³) = 1.806 × 10²³ ions.

qs.q: In the balanced ionic equation for the oxidation of iron(II) ions by permanganate ions in acidic medium: MnO₄⁻ + aFe²⁺ + bH⁺ → Mn²⁺ + cFe³⁺ + dH₂O, what is the value of coefficient b?
qs.e: The balanced half-equations are: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O and 5Fe²⁺ → 5Fe³⁺ + 5e⁻. Combining them gives: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. The coefficient of H⁺ (b) is 8.

qs.q: At high altitudes, liquid water boils at a temperature below 100 °C because:
o: The atmospheric pressure is lower than 1 atm, allowing vapor pressure to equal atmospheric pressure at a lower temperature
The vapor pressure of water increases dramatically with altitude
The intermolecular hydrogen bonds are weakened by lower gravity
The density of air is higher, increasing heat transfer rates
qs.e: Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of a liquid equals the external atmospheric pressure. At high altitudes, atmospheric pressure is less than 1 atm, so water boils at a lower temperature.

qs.q: A sample of gas has a volume of 2.00 dm³ at 27 °C and 1.00 atm pressure. Calculate its volume at 87 °C and 1.20 atm pressure.
Heating 2.50 g of hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals, CuSO₄·xH₂O, yields 1.60 g of anhydrous residue. What is the value of x? (Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Mass of water lost = 2.50 - 1.60 = 0.90 g. Molar mass of CuSO₄ = 160 g/mol. Moles of CuSO₄ = 1.60 / 160 = 0.010 mol. Moles of H₂O = 0.90 / 18.0 = 0.050 mol. x = 0.050 / 0.010 = 5. CuSO₄·5H₂O.

qs.q: According to collision theory, raising the temperature of a reaction system increases the reaction rate constant k primarily by:
o: Decreasing the activation energy barrier for the reaction
Increasing the total volume occupied by the reactant molecules
Shifting the reaction equilibrium toward the products
Increasing the fraction of reactant molecules with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
qs.e: Increasing temperature increases the average kinetic energy of molecules, exponentially increasing the fraction of molecules with energy exceeding the activation energy barrier (E_a).

qs.q: At a certain temperature, phosphorus pentachloride gas decomposes: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). If the degree of dissociation is 0.40 at a total pressure of P, express K_p in terms of P.
qs.e: Let initial moles of PCl₅ = 1. At equilibrium: PCl₅ = 1 - α, PCl₃ = α, Cl₂ = α. Total moles = 1 + α. With α = 0.40: total moles = 1.40. P_PCl₅ = (0.60/1.40)P, P_PCl₃ = (0.40/1.40)P, P_Cl₂ = (0.40/1.40)P. K_p = [P_PCl₃ × P_Cl₂] / P_PCl₅ = [(0.40/1.40) × (0.40/1.40) × P²] / [(0.60/1.40) × P] = (0.16 / 0.84) P ≈ 0.19 P.

qs.q: The standard enthalpy of neutralization for any strong acid reacting with any strong base in dilute aqueous solution is nearly constant (-57.3 kJ/mol) because:
o: Strong acids and strong bases have the same heat capacities
The net chemical reaction is simply the formation of water from hydrogen and hydroxide ions
The spectator ions absorb all the excess heat generated
The standard state conditions equalize all enthalpies of formation
qs.e: Strong acids and strong bases dissociate completely in water. The chemical reaction is simply: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l) (ΔH = -57.3 kJ/mol), with other ions remaining as spectator ions.

qs.q: When 4.0 g of solid sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is dissolved in 100 g of water, the temperature of the water rises by 10.0 K. Calculate the enthalpy of solution of NaOH. (Molar mass of NaOH = 40.0 g/mol, specific heat capacity of water = 4.18 J/g·K, neglect calorimeter heat capacity)
qs.e: Heat absorbed by water = m c ΔT = 100 g × 4.18 J/g·K × 10.0 K = 4180 J = 4.18 kJ. Moles NaOH dissolved = 4.0 / 40.0 = 0.10 mol. Enthalpy of solution (exothermic) = -4.18 kJ / 0.10 mol = -41.8 kJ/mol.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.10 mol/dm³ aqueous solution of a weak monobasic acid, HA, which has an acid dissociation constant, K_a = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵.
A buffer solution maintains a relatively constant pH when small amounts of acid or base are added. Its buffering capacity is maximum when:
o: The pH of the solution is equal to the pK_a of the weak acid
The concentration of the weak acid is double that of its conjugate base
The weak acid is completely ionized in the solution
The solution is highly diluted with distilled water
qs.e: By the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, pH = pK_a + log([conjugate base]/[weak acid]). When [base] = [acid], pH = pK_a, and the buffer is most resistant to pH changes in both directions.

qs.q: Which of the following mixtures of aqueous solutions will successfully form an effective acidic buffer solution?
qs.e: An acidic buffer consists of a weak acid (CH₃COOH) and its conjugate base salt (CH₃COONa), which resist changes in pH upon addition of H⁺ or OH⁻.

qs.q: What are the oxidation numbers of the two nitrogen atoms in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃, respectively?
qs.e: NH₄NO₃ consists of NH₄⁺ and NO₃⁻ ions. For NH₄⁺: N + 4(+1) = +1 → N = -3. For NO₃⁻: N + 3(-2) = -1 → N = +5.

qs.q: When chlorine gas is bubbled into a cold, dilute aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide, which of the following pairs of sodium salts is produced?
qs.e: Chlorine disproportionates in cold dilute NaOH: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl (sodium chloride) + NaClO (sodium hypochlorite) + H₂O. (In hot NaOH, NaCl and NaClO₃ are formed).

qs.q: A constant current of 9.65 A is passed through an electrolytic cell containing molten Al₂O₃ for 3000 seconds. Calculate the mass of aluminum deposited at the cathode. (Al = 27.0, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
Calculate the standard potential (E°_cell) for the reaction: 2Fe³⁺(aq) + Cu(s) → 2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cu²⁺(aq), given: E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V.
qs.e: In the reaction, Fe³⁺ is reduced (cathode) and Cu is oxidized (anode). E°_cell = E°_reduction - E°_oxidation = +0.77 V - 0.34 V = +0.43 V.

qs.q: When ethyne (acetylene) is treated with excess hydrogen gas over a finely divided nickel catalyst at 200 °C, the final product is:
qs.e: Ethyne undergoes complete catalytic hydrogenation in the presence of excess hydrogen: HC≡CH + 2H₂ → CH₃CH₃ (ethane).

qs.q: Which of the following organic reagents and conditions can be used to distinguish hexane from hex-1-ene in the dark?
o: Acidified potassium permanganate, which is decolorized by hexane only
Sodium metal, which reacts with hexane to release hydrogen gas
Tollen's reagent, which forms a silver mirror with hex-1-ene only
Bromine water, which is decolorized by hex-1-ene only
qs.e: Hex-1-ene is an unsaturated alkene. It undergoes rapid addition reaction with bromine water, decolorizing it immediately even in the dark. Hexane (saturated) does not react in the dark.

qs.q: The alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate with aqueous sodium hydroxide yields which products?
qs.e: CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + NaOH → CH₃COONa (sodium ethanoate) + CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol). This is a saponification-type reaction.

qs.q: An organic compound produces a yellow precipitate of triiodomethane (iodoform) when treated with iodine in sodium hydroxide solution. This compound could be:
qs.e: The iodoform test is positive for compounds with a CH₃CH(OH)- or CH₃CO- group. Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) is oxidized in situ to ethanal (CH₃CHO), which contains the CH₃CO- group, giving a positive test.

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes a major distinction between thermoplastic and thermosetting polymers?
o: Thermoplastics degrade chemically upon cooling to room temperature
Thermosetting plastics can be easily remolded and recycled several times
Thermosetting plastics have cross-linked structures and do not soften on reheating
Thermoplastics possess high density due to extensive cross-linking
qs.e: Thermosetting polymers (e.g., Bakelite) form permanent cross-links during curing and cannot be softened or remolded upon heating, whereas thermoplastics possess linear chains that soften when heated.

qs.q: Blister copper obtained from chemical smelting of copper pyrites is purified to high-grade copper (>99.99%) by electrolytic refining using:
o: An anode of pure copper, a cathode of crude copper, and an electrolyte of aqueous CuSO₄
Inert carbon electrodes with an electrolyte of molten copper chloride
A copper cathode, a platinum anode, and an electrolyte of dilute sulfuric acid
An anode of crude copper, a cathode of pure copper, and an electrolyte of aqueous CuSO₄
qs.e: In electrolytic refining of copper, the impure crude copper (blister copper) is made the anode and dissolves, while pure copper ions deposit onto the pure copper cathode.

qs.q: Rhombic sulfur (alpha-sulfur) and monoclinic sulfur (beta-sulfur) are allotropes of sulfur. What is the transition temperature at which they exist in equilibrium?
qs.e: Rhombic and monoclinic sulfur are in dynamic equilibrium at the transition temperature of 95.6 °C. Below this, rhombic is stable; above this, monoclinic is stable.

qs.q: Which of the following is the most abundant greenhouse gas in the Earth's unpolluted atmosphere?
qs.e: Water vapor is the most abundant natural greenhouse gas in the atmosphere, playing the largest role in the natural greenhouse effect, followed by carbon dioxide.

qs.q: Which indicator is most appropriate for the titration of a weak acid like ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) with a strong base like sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?
qs.e: The equivalence point for a weak acid-strong base titration is basic (pH ~8-10) due to salt hydrolysis. Phenolphthalein (pH range 8.3-10.0) is the most suitable indicator.

qs.q: What is the frequency of light emitted when an electron in a hydrogen atom undergoes a transition with an energy change of 4.00 × 10⁻¹⁹ J? (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)
Why is the first electron affinity of chlorine (-349 kJ/mol) more exothermic than that of fluorine (-328 kJ/mol) despite fluorine being smaller and more electronegative?
o: Fluorine's extremely small atomic size leads to high electron-electron repulsion in its compact 2p subshell
Fluorine has more electron shielding shells than chlorine
Chlorine is more electropositive and easily loses electrons
The nuclear charge of fluorine is too small to attract another electron
qs.e: Fluorine is very small, so its 2p valence shell has high electron density. Adding an electron experiences strong electron-electron repulsion, making the process less exothermic than in chlorine.

qs.q: Explain why carbon dioxide (CO₂) has a net dipole moment of zero while water (H₂O) has a net dipole moment of 1.84 D.
o: Oxygen is more electronegative in H₂O than in CO₂
CO₂ is linear and symmetrical, so polar C=O bond dipoles cancel out; H₂O is bent, so polar O-H bond dipoles reinforce
CO₂ contains non-polar covalent bonds whereas H₂O has polar bonds
Carbon dioxide has a crystalline lattice structure that locks dipoles
qs.e: CO₂ (O=C=O) is linear. The two polar C=O bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel. H₂O is bent, so its two polar O-H dipoles do not cancel, giving a net molecular dipole.

qs.q: What volume of 0.10 mol/dm³ KMnO₄ solution is required to oxidize completely 25.0 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ FeSO₄ solution in acidic medium? (MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O)
In a chemical synthesis of ammonia, the theoretical yield of ammonia is calculated to be 20.0 g. If the actual mass of ammonia collected is 16.0 g, what is the percentage yield?
qs.e: Percentage yield = (Actual yield / Theoretical yield) × 100 = (16.0 / 20.0) × 100 = 80.0%.

qs.q: Real gases show the greatest deviation from ideal gas behavior under which of the following sets of environmental conditions?
qs.e: At low temperature and high pressure, gas molecules are close together and move slowly, making molecular volumes and attractive intermolecular forces significant (violating ideal gas assumptions).

qs.q: Calculate the ratio of the root-mean-square velocity of hydrogen gas molecules (H₂, molar mass = 2.0) to that of oxygen gas molecules (O₂, molar mass = 32.0) at the same temperature.
qs.e: RMS velocity is inversely proportional to square root of molar mass: v_rms = √(3RT/M). Ratio v(H₂)/v(O₂) = √(M(O₂)/M(H₂)) = √(32.0 / 2.0) = √16 = 4.0.

qs.q: A 1.06 g sample of anhydrous sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is dissolved in water and allowed to crystallize, yielding 2.86 g of washing soda crystals. What is the formula of the crystals? (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Molar mass of Na₂CO₃ = 106 g/mol. Moles Na₂CO₃ = 1.06 / 106 = 0.010 mol. Mass of water in crystals = 2.86 - 1.06 = 1.80 g. Moles of H₂O = 1.80 / 18 = 0.10 mol. Ratio H₂O/Na₂CO₃ = 0.10 / 0.010 = 10. Formula: Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

qs.q: The first-order decomposition of a reactant has a half-life of 20 minutes. What length of time is required for 75.0% of the original reactant to decompose?
qs.e: If 75% decomposes, 25% remains. 100% → 50% (1 half-life) → 25% (2 half-lives). Total time = 2 × half-life = 2 × 20 min = 40 minutes.

qs.q: At a specific temperature, the equilibrium concentrations for the gas-phase reaction N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) are [N₂O₄] = 0.10 mol/dm³ and [NO₂] = 0.20 mol/dm³. Calculate K_c.
Calculate the enthalpy change (ΔH) for the reaction: H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g), using bond dissociation energies: D(H-H) = 436 kJ/mol, D(Cl-Cl) = 242 kJ/mol, D(H-Cl) = 431 kJ/mol.
qs.e: ΔH = energy of bonds broken - energy of bonds formed = [D(H-H) + D(Cl-Cl)] - [2 × D(H-Cl)] = (436 + 242) - (2 × 431) = 678 - 862 = -184 kJ.

qs.q: What is the pH of a solution prepared by mixing equal volumes of 0.10 mol/dm³ HCl and 0.10 mol/dm³ NaOH solution at 25 °C?
qs.e: Equal volumes of a strong monoprotic acid (HCl) and a strong monobasic base (NaOH) of the same concentration neutralize each other completely, producing a neutral salt (NaCl) solution with pH = 7.0.

qs.q: Which of the following compounds is produced when dry sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃) is heated strongly in a crucible?
qs.e: Thermal decomposition of sodium hydrogencarbonate: 2NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + H₂O(g) + CO₂(g)↑.

qs.q: During the redox titration of oxalic acid (H₂C₂O₄) with potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) in acidic medium, the oxidation state of carbon changes from:
qs.e: In H₂C₂O₄: 2(+1) + 2(C) + 4(-2) = 0 → 2 + 2C - 8 = 0 → 2C = 6 → C = +3. Carbon is oxidized to CO₂, where carbon is +4. The oxidation state changes from +3 to +4.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of magnesium (atomic mass = 24.3 g/mol) produced at the cathode when a constant current of 5.0 A is passed through molten MgCl₂ for exactly 1.0 hour. (1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
The standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) is assigned an arbitrary potential of 0.00 V under which of the following standard conditions?
o: 273 K, 1 atm pressure of H₂ gas, and 1.0 mol/dm³ OH⁻ ion concentration
298 K, 10 atm pressure of H₂ gas, and pure water
298 K, 1 atm pressure of H₂ gas, and 1.0 mol/dm³ H⁺ ion concentration
373 K, 1 atm pressure of H₂ gas, and 0.1 mol/dm³ H⁺ ion concentration
qs.e: Standard conditions for SHE require 298 K, 1 atm (or 1 bar) pressure of pure hydrogen gas, and an aqueous solution of 1.0 mol/dm³ H⁺ activity (or concentration).

qs.q: The chlorination of methane gas in the presence of ultraviolet light to yield chloromethane proceeds by which type of reaction mechanism?
qs.e: UV light splits Cl₂ into chlorine free radicals (initiation), which attack methane in propagation steps, substituting hydrogen atoms with chlorine (free-radical substitution).

qs.q: The anaerobic fermentation of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) by the enzyme zymase present in yeast cells yields carbon dioxide gas and which organic liquid?
qs.e: Fermentation equation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH (ethanol) + 2CO₂↑, catalyzed by zymase under anaerobic conditions at room temperature.

qs.q: The synthetic polyester Terylene (Dacron) is formed by the condensation copolymerization of which two monomeric species?
qs.e: Terylene is a polyester formed by condensation of terephthalic acid (benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid) and ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol), with elimination of water.

qs.q: The extraction of lead from its chief ore galena (PbS) involves roasting galena in air to form lead(II) oxide (PbO), which is then reduced to metallic lead by heating with:
qs.e: PbO is reduced in a blast furnace by heating with carbon (coke): PbO(s) + C(s) → Pb(l) + CO(g)↑, or PbO(s) + CO(g) → Pb(l) + CO₂(g).

qs.q: What is the chemical equation and gaseous product obtained when dry ammonium nitrate (NH₄NO₃) crystals are heated gently in a test tube?
o: NH₄NO₃(s) → NH₃(g) + HNO₃(g) yielding ammonia gas
NH₄NO₃(s) → N₂O(g) + 2H₂O(g) yielding dinitrogen monoxide gas
qs.e: Gentle heating of ammonium nitrate undergoes thermal decomposition to yield dinitrogen monoxide (laughing gas) and water vapor: NH₄NO₃(s) → N₂O(g) + 2H₂O(g).

qs.q: The major components of photochemical smog, which causes respiratory irritation and haze in urban areas, include:
o: Ozone, nitrogen oxides, and peroxyacetyl nitrates (PAN)
Sulfur dioxide, carbon dioxide, and soot
Carbon monoxide, argon, and water vapor
qs.e: Photochemical smog is formed by reaction of sunlight with nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds, yielding ozone, PAN, and aldehydes.

qs.q: Which of the following qualitative test papers turns a shiny silvery-black color in the presence of hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) gas?
qs.e: H₂S gas reacts with lead(II) ions on moist lead(II) ethanoate paper to precipitate black lead(II) sulfide (PbS), turning the paper silvery-black/black.

qs.q: Identify the correct set of principal (n) and azimuthal (l) quantum numbers for an electron occupying a 3d atomic orbital.
qs.e: For a 3d orbital, the principal quantum number n = 3. The orbital subshell letter corresponds to l: s=0, p=1, d=2, f=3. Hence, l = 2.

qs.q: How does the metallic (electropositive) character of elements vary down a group and across a period in the Periodic Table?
o: Decreases down a group, increases across a period
Increases down a group, increases across a period
Decreases down a group, decreases across a period
Increases down a group, decreases across a period
qs.e: Down a group, atomic size increases, so valence electrons are lost more easily (metallic character increases). Across a period, nuclear pull increases, making electron loss harder (metallic character decreases).

qs.q: The resonance hybrid structure of benzene (C₆H₆) accounts for which of the following physical and chemical properties of the molecule?
o: All six carbon-carbon bonds have the same length (0.139 nm), which is intermediate between a single and double bond
It undergoes rapid electrophilic addition reactions like alkenes
The molecule has a non-planar puckered ring conformation
It has an extremely low thermodynamic stability compared to hexatriene
qs.e: Benzene has six delocalized pi electrons over its planar ring. This resonance makes all C-C bonds equivalent in length (0.139 nm), and provides exceptional stability, favoring substitution over addition.

qs.q: What volume is occupied by 3.01 × 10²³ molecules of carbon monoxide (CO) gas measured at s.t.p.? (Avogadro's constant = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Moles of CO = (3.01 × 10²³) / (6.02 × 10²³) = 0.50 mol. Volume at s.t.p. = 0.50 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 11.2 dm³.

qs.q: In the electrolytic cell shown above containing aqueous copper(II) sulfate solution and inert carbon electrodes P and Q, what is the principal gaseous product liberated at Electrode P?
qs.e: Electrode P is connected to the positive terminal of the DC battery, making it the anode. In aqueous CuSO₄, OH⁻ ions and SO₄²⁻ ions migrate to the anode. OH⁻ ions are preferentially discharged due to lower discharge potential: 4OH⁻ → 2H₂O + O₂↑ + 4e⁻, liberating oxygen gas.

qs.q: In an acidic redox titration, 25.0 cm³ of 0.020 mol/dm³ potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) solution is found to react completely with 25.0 cm³ of an iron(II) sulfate (FeSO₄) solution. Calculate the molar concentration of Fe²⁺ ions in the sample. (MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O)
qs.e: Stoichiometric ratio: 1 mole of MnO₄⁻ oxidizes 5 moles of Fe²⁺. Moles of MnO₄⁻ = 0.0250 dm³ × 0.020 M = 0.00050 mol. Moles of Fe²⁺ = 5 × 0.00050 mol = 0.00250 mol. Molar concentration of Fe²⁺ = 0.00250 mol / 0.0250 dm³ = 0.100 mol/dm³.

qs.q: The solubility of silver chloride, AgCl, in pure water at 25 °C is 1.33 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³. Calculate the solubility product constant (K_sp) of AgCl at this temperature.
qs.e: AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq). Let solubility = s = 1.33 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³. K_sp = [Ag⁺][Cl⁻] = s × s = s² = (1.33 × 10⁻⁵)² = 1.7689 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol²/dm⁶ ≈ 1.77 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol²/dm⁶.

qs.q: The solubility product constant (K_sp) of barium sulfate, BaSO₄, is 1.10 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol²/dm⁶ at 25 °C. Calculate the molar solubility of BaSO₄ in a 0.10 mol/dm³ Na₂SO₄ solution.
