o: Nationalizing British Petroleum (BP) assets and Barclays Bank in Nigeria
Withdrawing from the United Nations General Assembly permanently
Imposing oil embargoes on all West African neighboring states
Expelling all diplomatic envoys from the Organization of African Unity
qs.e: Nigeria nationalized British Petroleum (BP) and Barclays Bank assets in 1979 to penalize the UK government for selling oil to apartheid South Africa and failing to enforce sanctions.

qs.q: The Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) brings together leaders of Commonwealth nations every two years to reach decisions based on
o: Veto power held by the British Monarch
Binding two-thirds majority voting in the UN Security Council
Proportional vote weight based on national GDP
qs.e: CHOGM operates on the principle of consensus rather than voting; all member states have equal voice regardless of size or economic wealth.

qs.q: The July 29, 1966 counter-coup in Nigeria was spearheaded primarily by Northern military officers who were motivated by
o: The desire to establish an Islamic Sharia state across Southern Nigeria
Rejection of the 1963 Republican Constitution's creation of Mid-Western region
Grievances over the killings of Northern leaders in January 1966 and opposition to Decree No. 34
A demand to transfer the federal capital from Lagos to Abuja immediately
qs.e: The July 1966 counter-coup arose from Northern anger over the selective assassinations of Northern leaders in January 1966 and General Ironsi's unification decree (Decree 34).

qs.q: Which principle of political culture explains why citizens in some traditional rural agrarian communities have virtually no awareness of central state governance institutions?
qs.e: In a parochial political culture, citizens have low or zero orientation toward central political systems and expect nothing from national institutions, identifying only with local tribes.

qs.q: The doctrine of Social Darwinism when applied to 19th-century political ideology was used primarily by colonial powers to justify
o: Imperial expansion and colonial subjugation of less developed societies
The abolition of private capital ownership
The creation of international judicial arbitration bodies
qs.e: Social Darwinism misapplied 'survival of the fittest' to human societies to justify European imperial conquest and racial subjugation as natural historical evolution.

qs.q: A major distinction between a written constitution and an unwritten constitution is that a written constitution is always
o: Flexible and easily amended by simple legislative resolutions
Embodied in a single comprehensive legal document drafted and adopted at a specific point in time
Derived entirely from unwritten judicial customs and conventions
Subject to automatic renewal every four years by executive decree
qs.e: A written constitution is a single, codified document created by a constituent assembly or constitutional convention, serving as supreme law.

qs.q: According to A.V. Dicey, the Rule of Law is undermined when administrative authorities are granted wide discretionary powers because wide discretion frequently leads to
o: Immediate dissolution of the National Assembly
Automatic repeal of all written criminal codes
Arbitrary exercise of power and unequal treatment of citizens
Compulsory military conscription of civil servants
qs.e: Dicey warned that wide discretionary administrative power leads to arbitrary decisions, undermining legal certainty and equality before the law.

qs.q: In parliamentary systems, the doctrine of 'collective responsibility' dictates that cabinet ministers must
o: Personally pay for budget overruns incurred by their departments
Submit to annual electoral recall petitions by constituents
Refuse to appear before legislative auditing committees
Publicly support all government decisions or resign from cabinet if they disagree
qs.e: Collective responsibility requires all cabinet members to publicly defend decisions made by cabinet; a minister who cannot support a decision must resign.

qs.q: The term 'guillotine motion' in legislative procedure refers to an executive or legislative motion designed to
o: Set a strict time limit on debate for various clauses of a bill to ensure a fast vote
Impeach the Chief Justice of Nigeria for judicial misconduct
Abolish the salary structure of local government chairmen
Suspend constitutional human rights during civil unrest
qs.e: A guillotine (or allocation of time) motion sets strict deadlines for completing debate on stages of a bill, cutting off further discussion when time expires.

qs.q: In public administration, delegated legislation in the form of 'Orders in Council' is issued by the
o: President of the Senate acting alone without executive consultation
Executive acting through the Head of State or Cabinet under statutory authority
Federal High Court when settling land tenure disputes
Chairman of the Federal Character Commission during general elections
qs.e: Orders in Council are executive orders issued by the formal executive (Head of State/Cabinet) pursuant to power delegated by parliamentary statute.

qs.q: The prerogative power of judicial review in Nigeria was famously upheld in the landmark case of Attorney General of Bendel State v. Attorney General of the Federation (1981), where the Supreme Court invalidated the Revenue Allocation Act because
o: The President signed the bill outside the geographical boundaries of Nigeria
The Governor of Bendel State refused to attend the State House of Assembly
The National Assembly failed to follow the mandatory constitutional legislative procedure required for passing money bills
The bill was drafted in English rather than local indigenous languages
qs.e: In AG Bendel State v. AG Federation (1981), the Supreme Court struck down the 1981 Allocation of Revenue Act because the National Assembly breached constitutional law-making procedure.

qs.q: Which commission recommended the establishment of the 'Special Constabulary' and local police forces in minority areas prior to Nigerian independence?
qs.e: The 1958 Willink Commission addressed minority fears by recommending non-discriminatory policing, national fundamental rights guarantees, and special development boards.

qs.q: The Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU), founded by Mallam Aminu Kano in 1950, positioned itself ideologically as a radical party advocating the
o: Emancipation of the poor masses (Talakawa) from feudal oppression and aristocratic rule in Northern Nigeria
Creation of an independent oil-producing sovereign state in the South
Immediate unification of Nigeria with the French West African colonies
Establishment of an absolute hereditary monarchy across the Middle Belt
qs.e: NEPU was a radical populist party that challenged traditional feudal aristocracy (Emirs/NPC) in Northern Nigeria, fighting for the political and social rights of the Talakawa.

qs.q: Which pressure group technique involves public demonstrations, peaceful marches, and distribution of handbills outside government headquarters to mobilize public opinion?
qs.e: Picketing is a public demonstration method where protesters gather outside workplaces or government buildings to draw public attention and apply pressure.

qs.q: Under the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system of proportional representation, voters rank candidates in multi-member constituencies using
o: A single checkmark next to the political party logo only
A compulsory oral declaration before the returning officer
Preferential numbers (1, 2, 3...) on the ballot paper
A binary yes/no vote on executive decrees
qs.e: STV is a preferential voting system in multi-member districts where voters rank candidates in order of preference (1st choice, 2nd choice, etc.).

qs.q: The concept of 'Bureaucracy' as an ideal administrative organization characterized by hierarchy, rules, impersonality, and technical competence was formulated by
qs.e: German sociologist Max Weber defined the classic model of bureaucracy based on rational-legal authority, specialization, hierarchy, and strict rules.

qs.q: The General Orders (now Public Service Rules) in the Nigerian Civil Service serve primarily as the
o: Codified administrative rules governing conditions of service, discipline, and conduct of civil servants
Statutory penal code enforced by federal military tribunals
Financial guidelines for state government local council elections
Standing orders of the House of Representatives during budget debates
qs.e: Public Service Rules (formerly General Orders) set out regulatory conditions of service, operational procedures, and ethical standards for civil servants.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, local government councils derive their statutory financial allocation from the Federation Account through the
qs.e: Under Section 162(6) of the 1999 Constitution, federal funds allocated to local governments in a state are paid into the State Joint Local Government Account.

qs.q: Which constitutional right guaranteed under Chapter IV of the 1999 Nigerian Constitution protects citizens against arbitrary arrest and unlawful detention by state security agencies?
o: Right to freedom of thought and conscience
Right to peaceful assembly and association
qs.e: Section 35 guarantees the Right to Personal Liberty, stipulating that no person shall be deprived of liberty except in accordance with procedures permitted by law.

qs.q: Nigeria's leadership role in establishing the Technical Aid Corps (TAC) scheme in 1987 under General Ibrahim Babangida was designed to
o: Deploy active military officers to enforce border controls across West Africa
Export raw crude oil at discounted prices to European Union countries
Establish offshore financial intelligence centers in Latin America
Provide Nigerian skilled manpower and technical assistance to developing African, Caribbean, and Pacific (ACP) nations
qs.e: The TAC scheme, launched in 1987, deploys young Nigerian professionals (doctors, teachers, engineers) to ACP countries as a tool of soft power and Afrocentric foreign assistance.

qs.q: The United Nations General Assembly decisions on important international questions (such as peace recommendations or budget approvals) require a
o: Two-thirds majority of members present and voting
Unanimous vote of all member states
Simple majority vote of the 5 permanent Security Council members
Consensus approval from the International Court of Justice
qs.e: Under Article 18 of the UN Charter, decisions on important questions in the General Assembly require a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

qs.q: The 1975 military coup that removed General Yakubu Gowon from power occurred while Gowon was attending an OAU Summit in Kampala. The coup leaders appointed as Head of State
qs.e: On July 29, 1975, General Gowon was overthrown in a bloodless coup while attending the OAU Summit, and Brigadier Murtala Muhammed became Head of State.

qs.q: The concept of 'rule by divine right' was historically used in political monarchies to claim that
o: Power resides exclusively in the elected representatives of the working class
The judiciary holds supreme veto power over royal succession decrees
The monarch derives political authority directly from God and is accountable to no earthly parliament
Local government councils must be elected through direct secret ballot
qs.e: The Divine Right of Kings asserted that monarchs derive sovereign authority directly from God, making royal decisions immune to earthly accountability.

qs.q: A core principle of Classical Liberalism is the belief in
o: Total state ownership of all industrial factories and land
The divine rule of traditional hereditary chiefs
Enforcing mandatory state religious doctrines through criminal courts
Minimal state intervention in individual economic activity and maximum personal liberty
qs.e: Classical liberalism emphasizes individual freedom, private property, free markets, and limited government interference in economic and personal life.

qs.q: The principle of 'constitutionalism' means that government power must be
o: Limited and bound by explicit constitutional rules and legal procedures
Vested entirely in a single military supreme commander during peace
Exercised without any possibility of judicial challenge in court
Derived strictly from decrees issued by regional traditional rulers
qs.e: Constitutionalism is the principle that government authority is derived from and limited by a supreme constitution, preventing arbitrary or tyrannical governance.

qs.q: Which legal document historically laid the foundation for civil liberties and limited royal absolutism in England in 1215?
qs.e: The Magna Carta (1215) forced King John to accept legal limits on royal power, laying early foundations for the Rule of Law and constitutional government.

qs.q: In a parliamentary system, if the executive branch dissolves parliament and calls early general elections, this action is taken by the Head of State on the advice of the
qs.e: In parliamentary governance, the Prime Minister has the constitutional prerogative to request the Head of State to dissolve parliament and trigger snap general elections.

qs.q: The legislative power to investigate financial corruption or maladministration in government ministries through special probe committees is called the power of
qs.e: Under Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution, the legislature holds investigative powers to inquire into public funds and expose corruption or inefficiency.

qs.q: The principle of 'fiscal federalism' deals primarily with the constitutional arrangements governing
o: The allocation of revenue-raising powers and expenditure responsibilities between tiers of government
The deployment of military forces during regional civil disturbances
The appointment of international judges to regional economic tribunals
The registration of political parties by central electoral commissions
qs.e: Fiscal federalism addresses financial relationships, revenue assignment, tax jurisdictions, and statutory transfers among different tiers of a federal government.

qs.q: The 1960 Independence Constitution of Nigeria differed from the 1963 Republican Constitution primarily because under the 1960 Constitution
o: The Supreme Court of Nigeria was the court of last resort
The Queen of England remained Nigeria's titular Head of State represented by a Governor-General
The President exercised absolute executive powers without a Prime Minister
Nigeria operated a unicameral central parliament in Lagos
qs.e: Under the 1960 Independence Constitution, Queen Elizabeth II was retained as Head of State (represented locally by Governor-General Azikiwe) until the 1963 Republican transition.

qs.q: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), formed in 1944 with Herbert Macaulay as President and Nnamdi Azikiwe as Secretary-General, was historically significant as a
o: Regional political party representing Western cocoa farmers exclusively
Pro-colonial advisory council organized by the British Governor
Vibrant nationwide nationalist movement seeking self-governance for Nigeria
Traditional religious movement in Northern Nigeria
qs.e: The NCNC was Nigeria's first major nationalist party with broad nationwide cross-regional membership, leading anti-colonial agitation across the country.

qs.q: In pressure group terminology, 'hyper-pluralism' describes a situation where
o: The government bans all non-governmental associations nationwide
Political parties merge into a single official state party
Local government councils operate without statutory budgets
So many competing pressure groups become powerful that government policy becomes gridlocked and contradictory
qs.e: Hyper-pluralism occurs when interest groups become so strong and numerous that government attempts to satisfy all of them, resulting in contradictory policies and political paralysis.

qs.q: The electoral system where voters cast a single vote for a party list, and candidates win seats strictly in the order they appear on the list, is called
qs.e: In closed-list proportional representation, political party leadership fixes candidate rankings on party lists, and voters cannot alter the order of candidates.

qs.q: The United Nations Security Council consists of fifteen member states. The five permanent members possessing absolute veto power over non-procedural resolutions are
o: United States, Germany, Japan, India, and Brazil
United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China
United Kingdom, France, Germany, China, and South Africa
Russia, China, India, Nigeria, and Canada
qs.e: The P5 permanent members of the UN Security Council established in 1945 are the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia (formerly USSR), and China.

qs.q: <svg width="300" height="150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="background:#fff;"><rect x="100" y="10" width="100" height="35" fill="#fff" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="32" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif">Federal Level</text><rect x="20" y="80" width="80" height="35" fill="#fff" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="60" y="102" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif">Exclusive</text><rect x="110" y="80" width="80" height="35" fill="#fff" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="102" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif">Concurrent</text><rect x="200" y="80" width="80" height="35" fill="#fff" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="240" y="102" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif">Residual</text><path d="M 150 45 L 60 80 M 150 45 L 150 80 M 150 45 L 240 80" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/></svg> Referring to the federal power structure tree in the diagram, if a new emerging technology arises that is omitted from both the Exclusive and Concurrent lists, which level of government holds constitutional authority over it?
o: Federal Government under implied exclusive powers
Local Government Councils under customary municipal powers
State Governments under residual legislative powers
Federal Executive Council by issuing administrative decrees
qs.e: Under federal constitutional jurisprudence, any legislative subject omitted from both the Exclusive and Concurrent lists automatically falls under the Residual List, which belongs exclusively to State Houses of Assembly.

qs.q: The landmark Supreme Court judgment in Attorney General of the Federation v. Attorney General of Abia State & Ors (2002) regarding the Off-Shore/On-Shore Dichotomy established that
o: Littoral states hold absolute ownership of all natural gas deposits up to 200 nautical miles into the continental shelf
Derivation funds must be paid directly to local government traditional councils rather than state treasuries
The Federal Government has no constitutional authority to levy customs duties on maritime imports
The seaward boundary of a littoral state extends only to the low-water mark, making off-shore natural resources federal property
qs.e: The Supreme Court ruled in 2002 that the southern boundaries of littoral states end at the low-water mark, vesting off-shore territorial waters and continental shelf resources exclusively in the Federal Government.

qs.q: Under Section 308 of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the executive immunity clause protects the President, Vice-President, Governors, and Deputy Governors from
o: Civil or criminal court proceedings and arrest during their tenure of office
Legislative impeachment probes initiated by the House of Assembly
Audits conducted by the Auditor-General of the Federation
Internal party disciplinary actions and expulsion
qs.e: Section 308 grants absolute constitutional immunity from civil or criminal court summons, prosecution, or arrest to incumbents of executive offices (President, VP, Governors, Deputy Governors) while in office.

qs.q: In the controversial 1979 Presidential Election dispute (Awolowo v. Shagari), the central legal question hinged on the mathematical interpretation of 'two-thirds of 19 states'. The Supreme Court upheld the election of Shehu Shagari by ruling that two-thirds of 19 states meant
o: 13 whole states rounded up to the nearest integer
12 states plus two-thirds of the votes cast in the 13th state (Kano State)
12 whole states without any fractional calculation
qs.e: The Supreme Court accepted the technical submission that two-thirds of 19 is 12 and 2/3, holding that FEDECO correctly declared Shagari elected since he met 25% in 12 states plus over 25% of 2/3 of votes in Kano State.

qs.q: The Mid-Western Region was created in August 1963 following a plebiscite and constitutional procedure. What made this state creation historically unique in Nigerian political history?
o: It was created via a military decree issued by the Supreme Military Council
It was formed by merging two Northern emirates with Lagos Federal Territory
It was the only region ever created strictly through democratic civilian constitutional process
It abolished the post of regional Premier and House of Chiefs
qs.e: Mid-Western Region was carved out of the Western Region in 1963 pursuant to Section 4 of the 1960/1963 Constitution, making it the only region created through peaceful civilian constitutional mechanics.

qs.q: Under the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria, the Federal Character Commission was established to ensure that
o: All registered political parties maintain identical campaign manifestos
The President selects ministers strictly from the military officer corps
Local government councils operate without central budgetary allocations
Appointments to public federal agencies reflect equitably the linguistic, ethnic, and geographic diversity of Nigeria
qs.e: The Federal Character Commission enforces the constitutional mandate (Section 14(3)) ensuring fair and equitable distribution of public posts and socio-economic infrastructure across all federating units.

qs.q: The 1988 Dotun Philips Civil Service Reform attempted to abolish which traditional administrative body and replace it with internal ministry personnel boards?
o: The traditional centralized Civil Service Commission recruitment role for middle cadres
The Public Accounts Committee of the House of Representatives
The Federal Character Commission monitoring unit
The National Judicial Council recommendation tribunal
qs.e: The 1988 reform decentralized staff recruitment, promotion, and discipline directly to individual ministries (under Ministerial Personnel Boards), undermining the traditional Civil Service Commission authority.

qs.q: In historical revenue allocation, the Hicks-Phillipson Commission of 1951 recommended four principles for sharing national revenue among regions. Which of the following was one of those principles?
o: Off-shore Exploration, Landmass, Terrain, and Population Density
Derivation, Need, National Interest, and Independent Revenue
Internal Tax Capacity, Inflation Rate, Foreign Reserve, and Trade Deficit
Military Budget, Judicial Salaries, Chieftaincy Stipends, and Port Tariff
qs.e: The 1951 Hicks-Phillipson Commission proposed four primary criteria: Derivation, Need, National Interest, and Continuity/Independent Revenue.

qs.q: During the 1993 transition program under General Ibrahim Babangida, the federal military government instituted a compulsory two-party framework. The two state-created political parties were the
o: People's Democratic Party (PDP) and All Progressives Congress (APC)
Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN) and National Party of Nigeria (NPN)
Social Democratic Party (SDP) and National Republican Convention (NRC)
Nigerian National Alliance (NNA) and United Progressive Grand Alliance (UPGA)
qs.e: Babangida's military regime established two grassroots political parties by decree: the SDP ('a little to the left') and the NRC ('a little to the right').

qs.q: The annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election (won by Chief M.K.O. Abiola) led to the resignation of General Babangida and the installation of an Interim National Government (ING) headed by
qs.e: Following intense public outrage over the June 12 annulment, General Babangida stepped aside in August 1993, appointing Chief Ernest Shonekan to head the short-lived Interim National Government.

qs.q: In November 1993, the Interim National Government led by Ernest Shonekan was declared illegal by a High Court judgment delivered by Justice Dolapo Akinsanya. Shortly after, the ING was overthrown by
qs.e: On November 17, 1993, General Sani Abacha forced Ernest Shonekan to resign, dissolved all democratic institutions, and established the Provisional Ruling Council (PRC).

qs.q: The Bakassi Peninsula border dispute between Nigeria and Cameroon was formally brought before the International Court of Justice (ICJ). In October 2002, the ICJ ruled in favor of Cameroon primarily based on the
qs.e: The ICJ awarded sovereignty over Bakassi to Cameroon in October 2002 based on the 1913 Anglo-German treaty, leading to the 2006 Greentree Agreement and peaceful transfer.

qs.q: Which international trade and economic agreement signed in 1975 established trade preferences between European Union nations and developing ACP (African, Caribbean, and Pacific) countries?
qs.e: The Lomé Convention (first signed in Lomé, Togo in 1975) established non-reciprocal trade preferences and aid frameworks between the European Economic Community and ACP states.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, a proposed amendment affecting fundamental human rights or state creation requires a special legislative threshold in the National Assembly of
o: Simple majority of members present and voting in a joint sitting
Two-thirds majority in Senate and simple majority in House of Representatives
Unanimous approval by the Federal Executive Council and Council of State
Four-fifths majority of all members of each house and approval by two-thirds of State Houses of Assembly
qs.e: Section 9(3) specifies that amending Section 8 (state creation/boundary adjustment) or Chapter IV (fundamental rights) requires an elevated four-fifths supermajority in both National Assembly houses plus approval by two-thirds of State Assemblies.

qs.q: The concept of 'Monism' in international law holds that international treaties signed and ratified by a state automatically become part of domestic national law. In contrast, Nigeria practices 'Dualism' (Section 12 of 1999 Constitution), meaning an international treaty
o: Has no force of law domestically unless enacted into law by the National Assembly
Is automatically superior to the 1999 Constitution upon executive signature
Must be approved by a national referendum before diplomatic signature
Applies strictly inside Federal Capital Territory Abuja
qs.e: Under Section 12 of the 1999 Constitution (Dualist doctrine), no international treaty or accord signed by the executive has force of law in Nigeria until the National Assembly enacts it into domestic statute.

qs.q: In the 1951 Macpherson Constitution, the central legislative body was called the House of Representatives. Members of this central house were selected through
o: Direct universal adult suffrage across all federal constituencies
Indirect election from the Regional Houses of Assembly acting as electoral colleges
Direct appointment by the British Colonial Secretary in London
Ex-officio nomination by traditional Emirs and Obas
qs.e: Under Macpherson's 1951 framework, members of the central House of Representatives were elected indirectly from among members of the Regional Houses of Assembly (acting as electoral colleges).

qs.q: The Mbanefo Salary Commission (1959) and Morgan Commission (1964) in Nigerian public administration were instituted primarily to address grievances regarding
o: The abolition of regional civil service recruitment boards
The nationalization of foreign commercial banks
Wage disparities, inflation, and public sector minimum wage adjustments
The re-alignment of local government council electoral boundaries
qs.e: These commissions evaluated public sector living standards, cost-of-living allowances, and minimum wage demands to resolve industrial agitation.

qs.q: The 1976 Local Government Reforms prescribed a specific demographic population threshold for establishing a standard Local Government Area in Nigeria. What was this range?
qs.e: The 1976 Reform Guidelines stipulated that a local government area should ideally cover a population between 150,000 and 800,000 to ensure administrative viability.

qs.q: In political science, the 'Iron Law of Oligarchy', formulated by sociologist Robert Michels, posits that
o: All complex organizations, regardless of how democratic they appear, inevitably develop leadership elites who dominate decision-making
Military regimes in developing nations automatically transition to stable multi-party democracies within five years
Proportional representation electoral systems eliminate all political corruption
Unwritten constitutions guarantee greater personal freedom than written constitutions
qs.e: Robert Michels argued that democratic organizations naturally succumb to elite control because organizational complexity requires specialized leadership, concentrating power in a few hands.

qs.q: Under the doctrine of parliamentary supremacy in the United Kingdom, parliament can enact or repeal any law whatsoever. In contrast, in Nigeria's constitutional democracy, supremacy resides in the
o: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
qs.e: Under Section 1(1) of the 1999 Constitution, the Constitution is supreme and its provisions bind all authorities and persons throughout Nigeria.

qs.q: The principle of 'Quo Warranto' is an extraordinary legal remedy issued by a superior court to
o: Force the President to sign an appropriation bill within 24 hours
Transfer a criminal murder trial from a State High Court to a Customary Court
Inquire by what legal authority an individual holds or exercises a public office or franchise
Order local government councils to lower market stall fees
qs.e: Quo Warranto ('by what warrant') challenges an individual who usurps or improperly holds a public office to demonstrate their legal authority to occupy that position.

qs.q: When the British colonial administration applied 'Indirect Rule' in Northern Nigeria through Lord Lugard, it utilized traditional native authorities. Why did Indirect Rule face severe operational failure when extended to Eastern Nigeria?
o: The Eastern Region possessed a highly developed industrial working class that rejected traditional chiefs
The British colonial office refused to fund warrant chiefs in Calabar
Islamic Sharia courts resisted the jurisdiction of British district officers
The Igbo society was traditionally decentralized and acephalous, lacking centralized hereditary monarchs
qs.e: Igbo political organization was republican and acephalous (decentralized). Imposing artificial 'Warrant Chiefs' created intense popular resentment, culminating in events like the 1929 Aba Women's War.

qs.q: The Aba Women's War of 1929 in Eastern Nigeria was triggered primarily by fears that the British colonial administration intended to
o: Extend direct taxation to women under the Warrant Chief system
Abolish Christianity and enforce traditional idol worship
Transfer palm oil plantations to Northern emirate rulers
Draft Igbo youth into the British Royal Navy
qs.e: The 1929 Aba Women's War was a major anti-colonial revolt sparked by census enumerations conducted by Warrant Chiefs, which women believed was a prelude to direct taxation.

qs.q: In the First Republic, the Action Group crisis of 1962 resulted from an intense ideological and personal rift between Chief Obafemi Awolowo and
qs.e: The 1962 AG crisis stemmed from tactical and ideological disagreements between party leader Awolowo (advocating democratic socialism and firm opposition) and Premier Akintola (advocating joining the federal ruling NPC coalition).

qs.q: Which major constitutional feature was introduced in the 1989 Constitution (Third Republic framework) to reduce ethnic polarization in party politics?
o: Abolition of the Senate and creation of a unicameral assembly
Rotational presidency mandated strictly by state origin
Establishment of a strict national two-party system
Creation of 774 local government areas in a single schedule
qs.e: The 1989 Constitution adopted Babangida's Political Bureau recommendation for a statutory two-party system (SDP and NRC) to force cross-regional coalitions and eliminate ethnic party enclaves.

qs.q: In legislative terminology, a 'filibuster' is an administrative tactic used in some assemblies where a legislator
o: Physically steals the mace from the legislative chamber during session
Signs an executive order overruling a judicial injunction
Submits a petition signed by 50% of registered constituency voters
Delivers excessively long speeches to prolong debate and obstruct or delay the final vote on a bill
qs.e: A filibuster is a obstructive parliamentary tactic where a legislator speaks continuously at length to stall or prevent a vote on a proposal.

qs.q: The Federal Character Commission, National Population Commission, and Independent National Electoral Commission are constitutionally classified as
o: Federal Executive Bodies under Section 153 of the 1999 Constitution
Ad hoc committees of the National Assembly Senate
Judicial tribunals established under Chapter VII
Non-governmental pressure groups registered under corporate law
qs.e: Section 153 of the 1999 Constitution establishes 14 independent Federal Executive Bodies, including INEC, NPC, and FCC.

qs.q: In administrative jurisprudence, the principle of 'Audi Alteram Partem' is a fundamental rule of Natural Justice requiring that
o: No person should act as a judge in a case where they have a personal interest
Both sides in a dispute must be given a fair hearing before an impartial tribunal before a decision is reached
Judicial decisions must be delivered in written English within 90 days
Legislative bills must be published in the federal government gazette three times
qs.e: Audi alteram partem ('hear the other side') is a core rule of natural justice stipulating that no person shall be condemned or penalized without a fair opportunity to present their defense.

qs.q: The second essential rule of Natural Justice, 'Nemo Judex In Causa Sua', mandates that
o: All accused individuals are presumed guilty until proven innocent by confession
Judges must be appointed exclusively by executive military governors
No person should sit as a judge in a cause in which they have a personal or financial interest
Appeals must be submitted to the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice
qs.e: Nemo judex in causa sua ('no one should be a judge in his own cause') prohibits bias, ensuring that adjudicators remain entirely disinterested and impartial.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, the power to create new Local Government Areas is shared between State Houses of Assembly and the National Assembly because
o: The Senate President must personally sign the local government charter
The Federal Character Commission must conduct a headcount in every new local ward
The Chief Justice of Nigeria must certify the financial viability of each council
The State Assembly enacts the law creating the local government, but the National Assembly must amend Part I of the First Schedule of the Constitution to give it formal effect
qs.e: While Section 7 grants State Assemblies power to create LGAs, Section 8(5) requires consequential constitutional amendment of the First Schedule by the National Assembly before new LGAs receive federal statutory allocations.

qs.q: The primary objective of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), established at the Belgrade Conference in 1961, was to ensure that developing nations
o: Maintained independence from superpower power blocs during the Cold War era
Adopted total economic isolation from international financial markets
Formed an international military alliance against the United Nations Security Council
Abolished national boundary borders across Africa and Asia
qs.e: NAM was created during the Cold War by leaders like Nehru, Tito, Nasser, and Nkrumah to safeguard national independence and avoid vassalage to either the US or Soviet power blocs.

qs.q: Under General Ibrahim Babangida's administration (1985–1993), the political bureau set up in 1986 recommended which political arrangement for Nigeria's Third Republic?
o: An absolute monarchy headed by a traditional ruler council
A social democratic state operating a two-party system
A multi-party parliamentary system modeled on the British House of Commons
A zero-party military diarchy lasting indefinitely
qs.e: The 1986 Cookey Political Bureau recommended a socialist-oriented democratic state operating a two-party system to curb ethno-religious political fragmentation.

qs.q: The concept of 'Asymmetric Federalism' describes a federal political system where
o: The central government exercises no legislative powers whatsoever over state borders
State governors are appointed directly by the federal Minister of Interior
Different constituent federating units possess unequal constitutional powers, autonomy, or special privileges
The legislature is composed entirely of non-elected traditional rulers
qs.e: Asymmetric federalism occurs when federating units do not hold identical powers—some regions or states enjoy distinct autonomy, tax powers, or linguistic privileges (e.g. Canada/Quebec, India/Jammu & Kashmir historically).

qs.q: In international relations, the term 'Deconcentrated Public Administration' refers to
o: The complete transfer of legislative authority to autonomous state governments
The sale of state public enterprises to private foreign investors
The merger of civil service departments with judicial courts
The delegation of operational administrative authority to lower levels within the same central ministry without granting political autonomy
qs.e: Deconcentration is an administrative form of decentralization where workload is redistributed from central ministry headquarters to field offices, retaining central political control.

qs.q: In contrast to deconcentration, 'Devolution' in administrative governance involves
o: The formal constitutional transfer of decision-making, legislative, and financial powers to autonomous sub-national governments
The central assignment of civil servants to regional post offices
The appointment of military task forces to collect state market rates
The nationalization of private commercial banking operations
qs.e: Devolution transfers real political, legislative, and financial authority to independent sub-national units (such as states or local governments) endowed with democratic mandates.

qs.q: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution designated which West African territory as a self-governing trust territory administered as part of the Federation of Nigeria until the 1961 plebiscite?
qs.e: Southern Cameroons was administered as a quasi-federal territory within Nigeria under the 1954 Constitution until the February 1961 UN plebiscite led it to join the Republic of Cameroon.

qs.q: Which major political party in the Second Republic was led by Alhaji Waziri Ibrahim and campaigned under the slogan 'Politics Without Bitterness'?
qs.e: Waziri Ibrahim broke away from the original NPP to form the GNPP in 1978, popularizing the famous motto 'Politics Without Bitterness'.

qs.q: In the 1979 Second Republic elections, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe emerged as the presidential candidate of the
qs.e: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe led the NPP in the Second Republic, winning governorships in Imo, Anambra, and Plateau states.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, the Code of Conduct Bureau (CCB) is empowered to
o: Receive asset declarations from public officers, enforce ethical standards, and prosecute violators at the Code of Conduct Tribunal
Conduct general elections for national legislative assemblies
Draft statutory annual budgets for state local government councils
Appoint judges to the Federal Court of Appeal
qs.e: The Code of Conduct Bureau enforces asset declaration compliance and ethical accountability across public offices, referring breaches to the Code of Conduct Tribunal (CCT).

qs.q: In comparative politics, 'Corporatism' is a system of interest representation where
o: Private business monopolies run all statutory judicial courts
Major peak interest organizations (such as key labor federations and industrial employer associations) are officially integrated into state policy-making processes
Political parties are legally forbidden from holding national conventions
The legislature is abolished and replaced by military council officers
qs.e: Corporatism structures interest representation by granting recognized peak bodies (labor, business) formal access to bargaining and decision-making alongside government state agencies.

qs.q: The concept of 'Gerontocracy' defines a governance system ruled by
o: Elders or senior members of society
qs.e: Gerontocracy is political governance where leadership is vested in elders who hold authority by virtue of age and traditional lineage.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the power to declare a State of Emergency in any part of the Federation is exercised by the President through a proclamation, which must be approved within two weeks by
o: A simple majority of the Council of State
Unanimous vote of all thirty-six State Governors
The Chief Justice of Nigeria acting alone
A two-thirds majority of all members of both the Senate and House of Representatives
qs.e: Under Section 305 of the 1999 Constitution, an emergency proclamation issued by the President ceases to have effect unless ratified by a two-thirds majority of all members of each house of the National Assembly.

qs.q: The 'Derivation Principle' in Nigerian revenue sharing reached its historical peak under the 1960 and 1963 Constitutions, when the percentage of mineral rents and royalties returned to regions of origin was set at
qs.e: Under the 1960 and 1963 Constitutions (Raisman formula), 50% of all mineral rents and royalties was paid directly back to the region from which it was extracted.

qs.q: In political sociology, 'Pluralism' views power in a democratic state as being
o: Monopolized entirely by a military executive junta
Dispersed among multiple competing interest groups rather than concentrated in a single ruling class
Vested exclusively in the central bank board of directors
qs.e: Pluralist theory posits that democratic political power is divided and bargained among various autonomous interest groups, preventing any single monolithic elite from dominating.

qs.q: Which major organ of the United Nations was established to oversee the administration of trust territories transitioning to independence, and suspended its operations in 1994 following the independence of Palau?
qs.e: The Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 after the last UN trust territory (Palau) achieved independence.

qs.q: The ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, Residence, and Establishment (1979) grants citizens of member states the right to enter other member states without a visa for a period of up to
qs.e: The 1979 ECOWAS Protocol grants citizens of ECOWAS states visa-free entry into member states for up to 90 days with valid travel documentation.

qs.q: In Nigerian political history, the 'Zangon Kataf' civil disturbances of 1992 and 'Tiv-Jukun' conflicts demonstrate the political challenge of
o: Managing ethno-religious conflicts and indigenous vs settler citizenship dynamics in local governance
Enforcing foreign economic embargoes imposed by the United Nations
Implementing proportional representation in single-member legislative constituencies
qs.e: These communal clashes highlighted intense friction over land ownership, chieftaincy institutions, and settler versus indigene status within local government areas.

qs.q: The 1922 Clifford Constitution created a Legislative Council for the Colony of Lagos and Southern Provinces, but laws for the Northern Provinces were made exclusively through
o: Debates in the Northern House of Chiefs
Proclamations issued directly by the British Governor
Statutes enacted by the British House of Commons
Decrees passed by local municipal councils
qs.e: Under the Clifford Constitution of 1922, the Legislative Council made laws only for Lagos and the Southern Provinces; the Governor legislated for the Northern Provinces by proclamation.

qs.q: The concept of 'Representative Democracy' is distinguished from 'Direct Democracy' because in a representative democracy
o: Every citizen votes directly on every piece of statutory legislation in open assemblies
The military high command selects cabinet ministers from university boards
Citizens elect delegates and lawmakers to make laws and govern on their behalf
Judges are appointed by popular local ward referendums
qs.e: Representative democracy relies on periodic elections where voters select representatives to exercise legislative and executive power on their behalf.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) is responsible for
o: Collecting customs duties directly at international seaports
Auditing the operational accounts of registered political parties
Fixing minimum interest rates for commercial financial institutions
Monitoring revenue accruals and proposing revenue allocation formulas to the National Assembly
qs.e: RMAFC (established under Section 153) monitors Federation Account revenues and periodically reviews revenue allocation formulas for federal, state, and local governments.

qs.q: The 'Preamble' to a constitution serves the primary legal purpose of
o: Declaring the guiding ideals, sovereign authority, and overarching objectives of the constitution
Listing the specific salaries of supreme court justices and military officers
Setting out the technical schedules for local government revenue collection
Granting absolute executive immunity to cabinet ministers
qs.e: A constitution's preamble outlines the philosophical foundations, source of authority ('We the People'), and fundamental goals of the nation.

qs.q: In administrative law, an action performed by a government official that exceeds the legal power conferred by enabling statute is void under the doctrine of
qs.e: Ultra vires ('beyond the powers') renders any administrative or legislative act null and void if it exceeds the statutory or constitutional power granted to that authority.

qs.q: The term 'Vote of Censure' in parliamentary proceedings differs from a 'Vote of No Confidence' because a vote of censure is aimed at
o: Dissolving the entire National Assembly and calling general elections
Striking down an unconstitutional judicial precedent set by the Supreme Court
Expressing severe parliamentary disapproval of a specific minister's policy without necessarily forcing the whole cabinet to resign
Suspending local government councils for financial audit queries
qs.e: A vote of censure expresses sharp reprimand toward a specific individual minister or policy, whereas a vote of no confidence targets the Prime Minister/Cabinet and collapses the government.

qs.q: In electoral administration, 'Malapportionment' occurs when
o: Foreign citizens are illegally registered to vote in border wards
Electoral commission officers alter physical ballot boxes during transit
Political parties fail to submit candidate lists before statutory deadlines
Electoral districts are drawn with wildly unequal population sizes, giving voters in smaller districts disproportionate legislative weight
qs.e: Malapportionment creates electoral districts with highly unequal voter populations, violating the principle of 'one person, one vote' by giving smaller districts disproportionate legislative power.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the National Assembly can pass a law on a subject not listed on the Exclusive Legislative List during which exceptional situation?
o: When the State House of Assembly of a state is unable to perform its legislative functions due to crisis or emergency
Whenever the President issues an unrecorded verbal request to the Senate
During routine annual budget review sessions
When a local government chairman requests federal police intervention
qs.e: Under Section 11(4) of the 1999 Constitution, if a State House of Assembly is incapacitated by crisis, the National Assembly may step in to enact laws for the peace, order, and good government of that state.

qs.q: Analyzing the evolution of revenue allocation formulas in Nigeria, the Aboyade Technical Committee (1977) introduced five technical criteria for sharing the Federation Account. Which of the following correctly identifies those criteria?
o: Derivation Percentage, Landmass, Continental Shelf Distance, Population Density, and State Capital Maintenance
Equality of Access to Development Opportunities, National Minimum Standards, Absorptive Capacity, Independent Revenue Effort, and Fiscal Efficiency
Primary School Enrollment, Hospital Bed Capacity, Internal Security Outlay, Border Length, and Inflation Differential
Export Volume, Port Throughput, Federal Highway Mileage, Chieftaincy Stipends, and Ecological Degradation
qs.e: The 1977 Technical Committee headed by Professor Ojetunji Aboyade rejected traditional subjective criteria and proposed five technical economic indices: Equality of Access, Minimum Standards, Absorptive Capacity, Independent Revenue Effort, and Fiscal Efficiency.

qs.q: The legal mechanics of military government in Nigeria were anchored on the doctrine of parliamentary and decree supremacy asserted in Decree No. 13 of 1970 (The Federal Military Government Supremacy and Enforcement of Decrees Decree). This decree was promulgated specifically to nullify which Supreme Court decision?
o: Attorney General of Bendel State v. Attorney General of the Federation (1981)
Lakanmi v. Attorney General of the Western State (1970)
qs.e: In Lakanmi v. AG Western State (1970), the Supreme Court ruled that the military takeover was a constitutional transfer of power and that military decrees could be reviewed by courts. General Gowon's regime responded by enacting Decree No. 13 of 1970, asserting absolute military decree supremacy over judicial review.

qs.q: In constitutional jurisprudence, the 1962 Privy Council ruling in Adegbenro v. Akintola overturned the Nigerian Supreme Court judgment regarding the removal of Premier Samuel Akintola by Governor Sir Adesoji Aderemi. The Privy Council held that
o: The Governor must act exclusively upon a formal resolution passed on the floor of the House of Assembly
Only the Prime Minister of Nigeria had authority to dismiss a regional Premier
The British Monarch was required to sign the dismissal instrument in person
The Governor could constitutionally remove the Premier based on evidence outside a formal parliamentary vote of no confidence
qs.e: The Privy Council ruled in Adegbenro v. Akintola (1963) that the Western Region Constitution did not explicitly stipulate that the Governor's assessment of a Premier losing majority support must be derived solely from a floor vote in the assembly. This prompted the regional government to amend the constitution retroactively to nullify the Privy Council decision.

qs.q: In the 1951 Macpherson Constitution, electoral mechanics for selecting members to the central House of Representatives utilized a multi-stage Electoral College system. In the Western Region, this electoral college hierarchy operated as
o: Primary Electoral Units to Intermediate Electoral Colleges, then to Divisional Electoral Colleges, and finally to the Regional House of Assembly
Direct secret ballot voting at municipal polling wards directly to the House of Representatives
Nomination by traditional Obas in Council directly ratified by the British Governor
A single national primary election organized by the Federal Electoral Commission
qs.e: The 1951 Macpherson framework operated a complex 3-tier to 4-tier indirect electoral college system where voters chose electors at primary levels, who then voted through intermediate/divisional colleges up to the Regional Assembly, which elected members to the central House.

qs.q: Comparing the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria regarding state creation mechanics, Section 8 mandates a multi-stage supermajority process. Which sequence of approvals is constitutionally required before a new state can be created?
o: Unanimous vote in Federal Executive Council -> Order-in-Council signed by President -> Ratification by simple majority in Senate

Request supported by 2/3 of members representing the area in Senate, House, and State Assembly -> Referendum approved by 2/3 of area population -> Approval by 2/3 of all State Houses of Assembly -> Resolution passed by 2/3 majority in National Assembly
Proclamation by National Judicial Council -> Approval by 3/4 of State Governors -> Resolution passed by House of Representatives
Direct executive order by President -> Referendum approved by simple majority of national voters -> Gazetting by Minister of Justice
qs.e: Section 8 specifies four rigorous stages: (1) 2/3 request by legislators representing the area; (2) Referendum approved by 2/3 of area voters; (3) Approval of referendum result by simple majority of all State Assemblies; (4) Approval by 2/3 supermajority in both houses of National Assembly.

qs.q: In political theory, the concept of 'Polyarchy', developed by American political scientist Robert Dahl, defines modern democratic governance as a political system characterized by
o: Absolute rule by a benevolent coalition of military and civilian technocrats
Direct legislation through weekly national electronic referendums
High levels of inclusiveness (universal suffrage) and high levels of open public contestation and opposition
A strict one-party regime that permits internal factional debate
qs.e: Robert Dahl used 'Polyarchy' to describe real-world procedural democracies that approximate democratic ideals through two key dimensions: broad political participation (inclusiveness) and vigorous open competition/contestation.

qs.q: Evaluating the ideological tenets of Antonio Gramsci's theory of political power, 'Cultural Hegemony' explains how the ruling capitalist class maintains political dominion primarily by
o: Deploying armed police and military forces to suppress trade union strikes
Manipulating currency exchange rates and central bank interest rates
Drafting rigid written constitutions that ban opposition political parties
Propagating values, norms, and culture through civil society institutions so that their interest is accepted as universal common sense
qs.e: Gramsci argued that the ruling class maintains dominance not merely through state coercion (domination), but through 'cultural hegemony'—shaping cultural institutions, media, and education so that bourgeois worldview becomes accepted as natural 'common sense'.

qs.q: In administrative history, the 1988 Dotun Philips Civil Service Reform introduced 'Professionalization' by stipulating that civil servants must spend their entire career within a single ministry. A primary structural flaw of this policy was that it
o: Destroyed inter-ministerial staff mobility and created rigid administrative silos lacking broad generalist administrative leadership
Abolished all permanent posts and replaced staff with military officers
Forced all civil servants to register as active members of the ruling political party
Transferred civil service wage payment responsibility to local government councils
qs.e: By confining civil servants to specialized single-ministry career tracks, the 1988 reform eliminated cross-ministerial transfers, resulting in severe administrative rigidity, loss of generalist administrative breadth, and functional silos.

qs.q: The Mbanefo Revenue Allocation Commission of 1960 modified the Raisman formula by adjusting the allocation of the Distributable Pool Account (DPA). The allocation percentages to the regions under Mbanefo were set as
o: Equal 25% share to each of the four regions including Mid-West
Northern Region 40/95, Western Region 24/95, Eastern Region 31/95
50% to Northern Region and 50% divided between Southern Regions
100% derivation returned directly to oil-bearing provinces
qs.e: The Mbanefo Commission retained the DPA system established by Raisman (1958) but adjusted regional shares out of 95 parts: North received 40/95, West 24/95, and East 31/95 (leaving 10/95 for Southern Cameroons prior to its exit).

qs.q: During the 1977–1978 Constituent Assembly debates in Nigeria, the most contentious constitutional controversy that almost collapsed the transition to the Second Republic was the debate over the
o: Creation of a unicameral National Assembly
Abolition of the Federal Character Commission
Establishment of a Federal Sharia Court of Appeal
Transfer of the federal capital from Lagos to Abuja
qs.e: The 1977 Constituent Assembly witnessed a fierce ideological impasse over a proposal to establish a Federal Sharia Court of Appeal, leading to a boycott by Northern delegates until a compromise was struck retaining State Sharia Courts of Appeal.

qs.q: In international peacekeeping jurisprudence, the ECOMOG intervention in Sierra Leone in 1997 to restore the democratically elected government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah was conducted under which legal authorization framework?
o: Article 51 of the UN Charter regulating individual NATO collective self-defense
A bilateral defense pact signed between Great Britain and the Organization of African Unity
A direct judicial mandate issued by the International Court of Justice in The Hague
ECOWAS Revised Treaty and ECOWAS Security Mechanism Protocols later endorsed retroactively by UN Security Council resolutions
qs.e: ECOMOG's intervention in Sierra Leone was spearheaded by Nigeria under ECOWAS regional security protocols to reverse the 1997 AFRC military junta, subsequently gaining UN Security Council endorsement.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, Section 143 details the 11-stage procedure for removing the President or Vice-President via impeachment. Which of the following correctly identifies a mandatory statutory threshold in this sequence?
o: Investigation of allegations by a 7-member panel appointed by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, followed by a 2/3 supermajority vote of all members in each House of the National Assembly to adopt the report
Approval of the motion by 3/4 of State Governors represented in the Council of State
A national referendum approved by a simple majority of registered voters
Direct judicial review and confirmation by the full bench of the Supreme Court
qs.e: Under Section 143, if the 7-member panel appointed by the CJN finds the President guilty of gross misconduct, each House of the National Assembly must consider the report and pass a resolution supported by at least two-thirds majority of ALL members to effect removal.

qs.q: In comparative electoral mechanics, the 'Droop Quota' formula used to calculate the threshold of votes required for electing a candidate under the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system is expressed as
qs.e: The Droop Quota is the standard quota in STV elections, calculated as: [Total Valid Votes / (Seats + 1)] + 1. It represents the minimum number of votes a candidate needs to guarantee election.

qs.q: Analyzing the 1959 Independence Elections, the Action Group (AG) attempted to broaden its regional political appeal beyond the Western Region by campaigning vigorously among
o: Commercial traditional emirs in the core Sokoto Caliphate
French-speaking merchant elites in Dahomey and Niger Republic
Minority ethnic communities in the Middle Belt (Northern Region) and Calabar-Ogoja-Rivers (Eastern Region)
Active military officers serving in the West African Frontier Force
qs.e: To transform into a national party in 1959, Awolowo's AG forged alliances with minority parties in other regions—supporting the UMBC in the Middle Belt and the COR State Movement in the East.

qs.q: The concept of 'Consociational Democracy', formulated by political scientist Arend Lijphart, prescribes a model of democratic governance for deeply divided plural societies. Its four key pillars are
o: Unitary centralism, First-Past-The-Post voting, Executive dominance, and Unicameralism
Absolute military oversight, Presidential veto, Two-party monopoly, and State religion
Direct referendum, Anarchist decentralization, Open-list voting, and Gerontocracy
Grand Coalition executive, Mutual Veto, Proportionality in representation, and Segmental Autonomy
qs.e: Lijphart's Consociationalism prescribes four institutional mechanisms to maintain stability in deeply divided ethno-religious societies: Grand Coalitions, Mutual Minority Veto, Proportionality across public sector/representation, and Segmental Cultural Autonomy.

qs.q: In Nigerian political history, the '8-Point Demand' passed by the Northern House of Assembly in May 1953 following the self-government motion crisis was essentially a proposal to transform Nigeria into a
o: Loose Confederation with a weak central agency and autonomous regions
Highly centralized Unitary State with a single parliament in Kaduna
Military diarchy headed by British colonial army officers
Unicameral socialist republic based on state ownership
qs.e: Fearing Southern domination after the 1953 Enahoro motion crisis and Kano riots, the Northern legislature passed an 8-Point Resolution demanding a loose confederation where central authority would be limited to a non-legislative central agency.

qs.q: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, the process for creating a new region or adjusting regional boundaries (Section 4) required a proposal passed by two-thirds of the federal parliament, approval by two-thirds of regional legislatures, and a
o: Decree signed by the President of the Supreme Court
Referendum in the affected area approved by at least 60 percent of eligible voters
Resolution passed by the Commonwealth Prime Ministers Conference
Unanimous vote of all traditional rulers in the Privy Council
qs.e: Section 4 of the 1963 Republican Constitution mandated that creating a new region required a referendum in the affected territory where at least 60% of registered voters approved the proposal (as demonstrated in the 1963 Mid-West referendum).

qs.q: Evaluating the structural mechanics of the 1976 Local Government Reforms, 'Statutory Revenue Allocations' were constitutionally mandated to be paid directly from the Federation Account and State Governments. The initial federal statutory contribution percentage set in 1976 was
o: 20 percent of the Federation Account and 25 percent of State revenue
50 percent of all mineral derivation royalties collected centrally
5 percent of the Federation Account and 10 percent of State internally generated revenue
1 percent of national customs import duties
qs.e: Following the 1976 reforms, the Federal Military Government allocated 5% of the Federation Account to local governments in 1976 (later increased to 10% in 1981 and 20% under Babangida), alongside 10% of state IGR.

qs.q: In administrative philosophy, 'New Public Management' (NPM), which influenced Nigerian public sector reforms in the 1990s and 2000s, advocates replacing traditional Weberian bureaucratic management with
o: Total military command structures and martial discipline in civil ministries
Strict lifelong career tenure and abolition of performance appraisal boards
Centralized state monopoly over all commercial agricultural and industrial production
Market-oriented principles, performance contracting, competition, privatization, and customer satisfaction metrics
qs.e: New Public Management (NPM) introduces private sector management techniques into public administration—focusing on market competition, outcome metrics, performance contracting, and decentralization.

qs.q: Under Chapter III of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, a person seeking citizenship by naturalization must satisfy strict conditions under Section 27. Which of the following is a mandatory constitutional requirement?
o: Continuous residence in Nigeria for a period of at least 15 years immediately preceding the application, and assimilate into the habits and customs of a local community
Marriage to a Nigerian citizen by birth for a period of not less than 3 years
Ownership of commercial real estate valued at over 100 million Naira
Service as an officer in the Nigerian Armed Forces for at least 5 years
qs.e: Section 27(2) requires a naturalization applicant to prove continuous residency in Nigeria for 15 years, good character, intention to reside permanently, and acceptability to the local community.

qs.q: The concept of 'Constructive Engagement', pursued by certain Western powers toward South Africa in the 1980s, was sharply opposed by Nigeria's foreign policy establishment because it
o: Demand immediate military invasion of South Africa by United Nations forces
Advocated gradual diplomatic dialogue with the apartheid regime rather than imposing mandatory international economic and military sanctions
Granted total nuclear capability to non-aligned West African nations
Expelled South Africa permanently from the Commonwealth of Nations
qs.e: US Reagan administration policy of 'Constructive Engagement' favored quiet diplomacy and trade with South Africa rather than punitive sanctions, which Nigeria denounced as covert support for apartheid.

qs.q: In the United Nations organ structure, the 'Uniting for Peace' Resolution (Resolution 377 A), adopted by the General Assembly in 1950, empowers the General Assembly to act when the Security Council
o: Unanimously votes to dissolve the International Court of Justice
Expels a permanent member for non-payment of annual membership dues
Fails to exercise its primary responsibility for international peace due to a lack of unanimity among its 5 permanent members (P5 veto deadlock)
Amends the UN Charter without holding a global international conference
qs.e: Resolution 377 A ('Uniting for Peace') allows the UN General Assembly to consider international security threats and recommend collective measures (including force) when Security Council P5 veto deadlock paralyzes action.

qs.q: During General Sani Abacha's military regime (1993–1998), Nigeria experienced severe diplomatic isolation and was suspended from which major international organization in 1995 following the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa and the Ogoni 9?
o: The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
qs.e: Following the execution of environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight Ogoni leaders in November 1995, the Commonwealth Heads of Government suspended Nigeria's membership at the Auckland CHOGM.

qs.q: Analyzing the political ideology of Democratic Centralism, formulated by Vladimir Lenin, decision-making within the party structure is governed by the principle that
o: Members are free to debate and discuss policy internally, but once a decision is voted and taken by the majority, all members must strictly obey and implement it
Local party branches exercise absolute veto power over decisions made by the central committee
General elections must be conducted using direct universal suffrage without party screening
The judiciary holds supreme authority to strike down central committee directives
qs.e: Lenin's 'Democratic Centralism' combines internal democratic freedom of discussion ('freedom of discussion') with absolute unity of action ('unity of action') once the central party authority adopts a decision.

qs.q: Regarding the legislative procedure for adopting a new revenue allocation formula submitted by RMAFC under Section 162 of the 1999 Constitution, which requirement must be satisfied before the formula becomes law?
o: The Chief Justice of Nigeria signs the formula instrument into law by judicial order
The President lays the RMAFC proposal before the National Assembly, which enacts an Act of the National Assembly after considering the proposal
A national referendum is conducted across all 774 local government areas
The 36 State Governors unanimously ratify the document in the National Economic Council
qs.e: Under Section 162(2), the President tables the proposal from RMAFC before the National Assembly, which then enacts an Act of the National Assembly defining the revenue allocation formula.

qs.q:
Refer to the drainage pattern diagram below.

The river drainage pattern illustrated in the diagram, characterized by tributaries joining the main stream at acute angles like branches of a tree, is known as
qs.e: Dendritic drainage patterns resemble the branching tree system and develop on rocks of uniform resistance to erosion. Tributaries join the main stream at acute angles.

qs.q: If a straight road measures 6.5 cm on a topographical map drawn to a scale of 1:100,000, what is the actual ground distance in kilometres?
qs.e: At a scale of 1:100,000, 1 cm on the map represents 100,000 cm on the ground. Since 100,000 cm = 1,000 m = 1 km, 1 cm = 1 km. Therefore, 6.5 cm equals 6.5 km on the ground.

qs.q: When solar noon (12:00 PM) occurs at Greenwich (0° longitude), what is the local solar time at a place situated on longitude 15°E?
qs.e: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, which means 15° equals 1 hour. Places east of Greenwich are ahead in time. Moving 15° East adds 1 hour to Greenwich time (12:00 PM + 1 hour = 1:00 PM).

qs.q: Which of the following rocks is formed through the cooling and solidification of molten magma beneath the earth's surface?
qs.e: Granite is a intrusive (plutonic) igneous rock formed beneath the earth's surface from slow cooling magma. Basalt is extrusive, while sandstone and limestone are sedimentary rocks.

qs.q: The physical weathering process predominant in hot desert regions caused by repeated heating during the day and cooling at night is termed
qs.e: Exfoliation (thermal expansion and contraction) occurs in hot deserts where large diurnal temperature ranges cause outer rock layers to expand by day and contract by night, peeling off in layers.

qs.q: A steep-sided, steep-gradient valley with a narrow floor shaped by rapid vertical river erosion in its upper course is called a
qs.e: V-shaped valleys are carved by vertical downcutting of streams in their upper courses where water speed and vertical river bed erosion dominate lateral erosion.

qs.q: The extremely slow, downward movement of soil and rock debris down a gentle slope under the influence of gravity is known as
qs.e: Soil creep is the slowest form of mass wasting (mass movement), occurring imperceptibly down gentle slopes aided by freeze-thaw cycles and wetting-drying phases.

qs.q: The cold ocean current flowing southwards along the northwestern coast of Africa that exerts a desiccating effect on the Sahara Desert is the
qs.e: The Canary Current is a cold ocean current off NW Africa that cools lower air layers, creating atmospheric stability and reducing humidity, contributing to Saharan aridity.

qs.q: If the air temperature at sea level is 30.0°C, what will be the estimated air temperature at an altitude of 1,000 metres assuming an environmental lapse rate of 6.5°C per 1,000 metres?
qs.e: Temperature decreases with altitude at the lapse rate of 6.5°C per 1,000 m. Thus, at 1,000 m altitude, temperature = 30.0°C - 6.5°C = 23.5°C.

qs.q: The natural vegetation zone of Nigeria characterized by tall grasses, scattered deciduous trees like baobab and acacia, and distinct wet and dry seasons is the
qs.e: The Savanna vegetation belt covers over half of Nigeria, featuring drought-resistant grass cover interspersed with trees adapted to seasonal rainfall patterns.

qs.q: In a well-developed soil profile, the uppermost layer containing rich decomposed organic material known as humus is the
qs.e: The A horizon (topsoil) contains organic humus mixed with mineral particles, making it dark and fertile compared to the subsoil (B horizon) and parent material (C horizon).

qs.q: A region has a total population of 10,000,000 people and a total land area of 50,000 square kilometres. What is its arithmetic population density?
qs.e: Arithmetic population density = Total Population / Total Land Area = 10,000,000 / 50,000 = 200 persons per square kilometre.

qs.q: A long, continuous line of houses developed along a major highway, river bank, or railway track forms what type of settlement pattern?
qs.e: Linear settlements grow along linear transport or natural features like roads, river banks, canals, or railway lines due to ease of accessibility.

qs.q: Which of the following represents a major push factor encouraging rural residents in Nigeria to migrate to urban centers like Lagos and Abuja?
o: Inadequate employment and soil degradation in rural areas
qs.e: Push factors are negative conditions in rural areas that force people away, such as lack of economic opportunities, poor soil fertility, and inadequate rural infrastructure.

qs.q: The farming system in which farmers clear a plot of land, cultivate it for a few seasons, and abandon it to regain fertility naturally while moving to a new plot is called
qs.e: Bush fallowing (or land rotation/shifting cultivation) relies on resting cleared agricultural plots over a period of fallow years to restore soil fertility naturally.

qs.q: Nigeria's major commercial deposits of crude oil and natural gas are predominantly concentrated in which major physiological and geographical region?
qs.e: The Niger Delta coastal basin and offshore continental shelf hold Nigeria's extensive petroleum and natural gas reserves formed in thick deltaic sedimentary rocks.

qs.q: Which factor is most critical in determining the location of heavy weight-losing manufacturing industries like iron smelting and cement production?
qs.e: Weight-losing industries reduce bulk or weight during processing. Siting near raw material sources minimizes heavy transport costs for bulky raw inputs.

qs.q: Which transport mode provides the most economical means for bulk transportation of heavy raw materials like crude petroleum across long inland overland distances?
qs.e: Pipelines offer continuous, high-capacity, low operational cost movement of liquid and gaseous fluids like crude oil over long land distances.

qs.q: A country whose monetary value of visible physical goods exported exceeds the monetary value of visible physical goods imported experiences a
qs.e: A favorable (surplus) balance of trade occurs when visible commodity export revenues exceed visible commodity import expenditures.

qs.q: The highest mountain peak in Nigeria, reaching an elevation of 2,419 metres above sea level along the eastern border with Cameroon, is
qs.e: Chappal Waddi (Gangirwal) located in the Shebshi Mountains of Taraba State on the Cameroon border is Nigeria's highest elevation point at 2,419 m.

qs.q: On a contoured topographical map, brown contour lines drawn extremely close together indicate the presence of a
qs.e: Closely spaced contours represent rapid change in elevation over short horizontal distance, indicating a steep slope, escarpment, or cliff.

qs.q: Calculate the gradient of a hill slope if the vertical interval (difference in height) is 50 metres and the horizontal distance between the two points is 1,000 metres.
qs.e: Gradient = Vertical Interval / Horizontal Distance = 50 m / 1,000 m = 1 / 20, which is expressed as a ratio of 1 in 20.

qs.q: In a standard station climate graph, monthly precipitation (rainfall) amounts are conventionally represented using
qs.e: Climate graphs display monthly total rainfall as vertical bar charts (columns) while monthly mean temperatures are plotted as a continuous line.

qs.q: A map scale expressed as a Representative Fraction (R.F.) of 1:25,000 corresponds to which statement scale?
qs.e: Since 1:25,000 means 1 cm on map = 25,000 cm on ground, and 25,000 cm = 250 m (dividing by 100), the statement scale is 1 cm represents 250 metres.

qs.q: The primary cause of the annual occurrence of four distinct seasons (spring, summer, autumn, winter) on Earth is the
o: revolution of Earth around the Sun on a tilted axis
rotation of Earth on its axis in 24 hours
varying distance between Earth and Sun
qs.e: Earth's revolution around the Sun every 365.25 days combined with its axial tilt of 23.5° causes variations in sun angle and day length, creating seasons.

qs.q: Which sedimentary rock, formed primarily from accumulated calcium carbonate shells of marine organisms, transforms into marble under heat and pressure?
qs.e: Limestone is an organically formed sedimentary rock made of calcite ($	ext{CaCO}_3$). Under thermal metamorphism, limestone recrystalizes into marble.

qs.q: The chemical weathering process whereby carbonic acid in rainwater reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone rocks to form soluble calcium bicarbonate is
qs.e: Carbonation occurs when dissolved atmospheric $	ext{CO}_2$ forms weak carbonic acid ($	ext{H}_2	ext{CO}_3$) which converts insoluble limestone ($	ext{CaCO}_3$) into soluble calcium bicarbonate.

qs.q: Glacial erosion creates a steep-sided, flat-bottomed trough known as a
qs.e: Glaciers erode pre-existing river valleys by plucking and abrasion, widening and deepening them into characteristic U-shaped glacial troughs.

qs.q: A crescent-shaped lake formed in a abandoned river meander channel on a lower course floodplain is known as an
qs.e: When a river cuts through a narrow meander neck during high discharge, deposition seals off the old loop, forming a stagnant oxbow lake.

qs.q: Which atmospheric instrument is housed inside a white wooden louvered box called a Stevenson Screen to measure shade air temperature?
qs.e: Maximum and minimum thermometers (as well as wet and dry bulb psychrometers) are housed inside a louvered Stevenson Screen to prevent direct solar radiation.

qs.q: Trees in the tropical high rainforest of southern Nigeria feature large flared buttress roots primarily to
o: support tall heavy trees in shallow wet soils
qs.e: Buttress roots provide mechanical support for tall rainforest trees rooted in shallow topsoils subject to heavy rains and rapid nutrient leaching.

qs.q: Soils with high proportions of coarse sand grains have high permeability because they possess
qs.e: Sandy soils consist of large particles that create coarse, interconnected macropores allowing rapid gravitational water drainage and high permeability.

qs.q: The major hydroelectric power (HEP) station located on the River Niger in Niger State, forming Nigeria's largest artificial reservoir lake, is the
qs.e: Kainji Dam on the River Niger was commissioned in 1968 creating Lake Kainji, serving as Nigeria's pioneer large-scale hydroelectric facility.

qs.q: Which mineral resource, mined extensively around Enugu in southeastern Nigeria, historically supplied fuel for Nigerian railways and thermal power generation?
qs.e: Sub-bituminous coal deposits at Udi Hills in Enugu were discovered in 1909 and mined to power steam locomotives and the Oji River thermal power plant.

qs.q: The back bearing of a line whose true forward bearing is 045° is
qs.e: To find back bearing when forward bearing is less than 180°, add 180°: 045° + 180° = 225°.

qs.q: A rectangular forest reserve covers an area of 4.0 square centimetres on a map drawn to a scale of 1:50,000. What is the actual ground area of the forest reserve in square kilometres?
qs.e: On a 1:50,000 map, 1 cm = 50,000 cm = 0.5 km. Therefore, 1 sq cm on map = 0.5 km × 0.5 km = 0.25 sq km on ground. An area of 4.0 sq cm = 4.0 × 0.25 = 1.0 sq km.
